bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第112卷 卷第一百一十二 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 112, Roll 112.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 112, Roll 112.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十四】 起重光赤奮若，盡玄黓攝提格，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 34] From Chongguang Chifenruo through Xuanyi Shetige; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 34] From Chongguang Chifenruo through Xuanyi Shetige—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝丁隆安五年（辛丑，公元四零一年） 。

translations.literal: Fifth year of Long'an of Emperor An (xinchou, AD 401).
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year of Long'an of Emperor An (xinchou, AD 401).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，武威王利鹿孤欲稱帝，群臣皆勸之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Prince of Wuwei, Lilugu, wished to declare himself emperor, and all his ministers urged him to do so.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Prince of Wuwei Lilugu wished to take the imperial title, and his ministers all urged him on.

sentences.zh: 安國將軍瑜勿侖曰：「吾國自上世以來，被發左衽，無冠帶之飾，逐水草遷徙，無城郭室廬，故能雄視沙漠，抗衡中夏。

translations.literal: General of Pacifying the State Yugulun said: "Since antiquity our state has worn disheveled hair and garments fastened on the left, without caps or sashes; we follow water and grass in migration, without walled cities or houses—thus we could dominate the desert and contend with the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: General of Pacifying the State Yugulun said: "From antiquity our people have gone with loose hair and left-fastened dress, without caps or belts, moving with pasture and water and living without walls or houses—by that we have held the desert and stood against the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 今舉大號，誠順民心。

translations.literal: Now to raise a great title truly accords with the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a grand title now would indeed follow the people's wish.

sentences.zh: 然建都立邑，難以避患，儲畜倉庫，啟敵人心。

translations.literal: Yet to build a capital and establish towns makes it hard to avoid calamity; storing grain in granaries stirs the enemy's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet founding a capital and fixed settlements will not keep trouble away, and stockpiling in storehouses only provokes our foes.

sentences.zh: 不如處晉民於城郭，勸課農桑以供資儲，帥國人以習戰射。

translations.literal: It would be better to settle Jin people in walled places, urge them to farm and raise silkworms to supply stores, and lead our countrymen to practice fighting and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Better to settle Jin subjects in walled towns, set them to farming and sericulture for supplies, and keep our own people trained in war and archery.

sentences.zh: 鄰國弱則乘之，強則避之，此久長之良策也。

translations.literal: When neighboring states are weak, ride upon them; when strong, avoid them—this is a good long-term policy.
translations.idiomatic: Strike when neighbors are weak and withdraw when they are strong—that is the policy that lasts.

sentences.zh: 且虛名無實，徒足為世之質的，將安用之！」

translations.literal: Moreover an empty name without substance only suffices to make one a target for the world—of what use would it be!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, an empty title without substance only makes us a mark for the world—what good is that?"

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤曰：「安國之言是也。」

translations.literal: Lilugu said: "Pacifying the State speaks rightly."
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu said, "The Pacifying State is right."

sentences.zh: 乃更稱河西王，以廣武公辱檀為都督中外諸軍事、涼州牧、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He then instead styled himself Prince of Hexi and appointed Duke of Guangwu Rutan as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Governor of Liang Province, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He took the title Prince of Hexi instead and made Duke of Guangwu Rutan commander of all armies, Governor of Liang, and overseer of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，孫恩出浹口，攻句章，不能拔。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi, Sun En came out of Jiakou and attacked Gouzhang but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi, Sun En issued from Jiakou and besieged Gouzhang without success.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之擊之，恩復走入海。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi struck him, and En again fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi attacked him, and En fled back to sea.

sentences.zh: 秦王興使乞伏乾歸還鎮苑川，盡以其故部眾配之。

translations.literal: King of Qin Yao Xing sent Qifu Gangui back to garrison Yuanchuan and assigned him all his former followers.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing of Qin sent Qifu Gangui back to hold Yuanchuan and gave him his entire former following.

sentences.zh: 涼王纂嗜酒好獵，太常楊穎諫曰：「陛下應天受命，當以道守之。

translations.literal: King of Liang Zuan was addicted to wine and fond of hunting. Minister of Ceremonies Yang Ying remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty received the mandate in response to Heaven and ought to keep it by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: King Zuan of Liang drank heavily and loved the hunt. Minister of Ceremonies Yang Ying admonished him: "Your Majesty received Heaven's mandate and should uphold it through the Way.

sentences.zh: 今疆宇日蹙，崎嶇二嶺之間，陛下不兢兢夕惕以恢弘先業，而沈湎游畋，不以國家為事，臣竊危之。」

translations.literal: Now the realm daily shrinks, confined between two rugged ranges; Your Majesty does not daily stand in awe and nightly take caution to expand the former enterprise, but sinks in pleasure and roaming hunts and does not make the state your business—I privately fear for this."
translations.idiomatic: Our domain shrinks day by day, hemmed between two mountain chains; yet Your Majesty does not watch and guard night and day to enlarge your fathers' work, but drowns in drink and the chase and neglects the realm—I fear for us all."

sentences.zh: 纂遜辭謝之，然猶不悛。

translations.literal: Zuan with humble words thanked him, yet still did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan apologized humbly but did not change his ways.

sentences.zh: 番禾太守呂超擅擊鮮卑思盤，思盤遣其弟乞珍訴於纂，纂命超及思盤皆入朝。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Fanhe, Lü Chao, on his own authority attacked the Xianbei chief Sipan; Sipan sent his younger brother Qizhen to plead before Zuan, and Zuan ordered both Chao and Sipan to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao, governor of Fanhe, attacked the Xianbei leader Sipan without authorization; Sipan sent his brother Qizhen to complain to Zuan, who summoned both Chao and Sipan to court.

sentences.zh: 超懼，至姑臧，深自結於殿中監杜尚。

translations.literal: Chao was afraid; when he reached Guzang he closely attached himself to the Palace Attendant Du Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, in fear, reached Guzang and cultivated a close tie with Palace Attendant Du Shang.

sentences.zh: 纂見超，責之曰：「卿恃兄弟桓桓，乃敢欺吾。

translations.literal: When Zuan saw Chao he reproached him, saying: "You rely on your brothers' martial bearing and dare deceive me.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan received Chao and rebuked him: "You trust in your brothers' might and dare cheat me.

sentences.zh: 要當斬卿，天下乃定！」

translations.literal: I must behead you—only then will the realm be settled!"
translations.idiomatic: I ought to cut off your head—only then will the realm be at peace!"

sentences.zh: 超頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chao bowed his head and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Chao kowtowed and pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 纂本以恐愒超，實無意殺之。

translations.literal: Zuan had originally meant only to frighten Chao and had no real intention of killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had only meant to intimidate Chao and did not truly intend to kill him.

sentences.zh: 因引超、思盤及群臣同宴於內殿。

translations.literal: He then led Chao, Sipan, and the ministers to feast together in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Chao, Sipan, and the ministers to a banquet in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 超兄中領軍隆數勸纂酒，纂醉，乘步挽車，將超等游禁中。

translations.literal: Chao's elder brother, Central Army Commander Long, repeatedly urged wine on Zuan; Zuan became drunk, mounted a hand-drawn carriage, and took Chao and the others touring within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's brother Long, central army commander, kept pressing wine on Zuan until he was drunk; Zuan rode a hand-drawn cart and led Chao and the others through the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 至琨華堂東閣，車不得過，纂親將竇川、駱騰倚劍於壁，推車過閤。

translations.literal: When they reached the eastern wing of Kunhua Hall the carriage could not pass; Zuan's personal generals Dou Chuan and Luo Teng leaned swords against the wall and pushed the carriage through the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the east wing of Kunhua Hall the cart could not pass; Zuan's bodyguards Dou Chuan and Luo Teng set their swords against the wall and shoved the cart through the doorway.

sentences.zh: 超取劍擊纂，纂下車禽超，超刺纂洞胸；

translations.literal: Chao seized a sword and struck Zuan; Zuan left the carriage to seize Chao, and Chao stabbed Zuan through the chest;
translations.idiomatic: Chao grabbed a sword and struck at Zuan; Zuan leapt down to seize him, and Chao ran Zuan through the chest;

sentences.zh: 川、騰與超格戰，超殺之。

translations.literal: Chuan and Teng crossed blades with Chao, and Chao killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan and Teng fought Chao hand to hand, and Chao killed them both.

sentences.zh: 纂後楊氏命禁兵討超，杜尚止之，皆捨仗不戰。

translations.literal: Zuan's consort, Lady Yang, ordered the palace guard to punish Chao; Du Shang stopped them, and all laid down their weapons and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's queen, Lady Yang, ordered the palace troops against Chao, but Du Shang held them back and all dropped their arms without fighting.

sentences.zh: 將軍魏益多入，取纂首，楊氏曰：「人已死，如土石，無所復知，何忍復殘其形骸乎！」

translations.literal: General Wei Yiduo entered and took Zuan's head; Lady Yang said: "The man is already dead, like earth and stone—he can know nothing more; how can you bear to mutilate his body further!"
translations.idiomatic: General Wei Yiduo came in and took Zuan's head. Lady Yang said, "He is dead as clay and knows nothing—how can you bear to mutilate his body!"

sentences.zh: 益多罵之，遂取纂首以徇，曰：「纂違先帝之命，殺太子而自立，荒淫暴虐。

translations.literal: Yiduo reviled her, then took Zuan's head and displayed it, saying: "Zuan defied the former emperor's command, killed the crown prince, and set himself up; he was dissolute and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Yiduo cursed her, then paraded Zuan's head, proclaiming, "Zuan defied the late emperor, murdered the heir, and seized the throne; he was lewd and tyrannical.

sentences.zh: 番禾太守超順人心而除之，以安宗廟。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Fanhe, Chao, followed the people's hearts in removing him to settle the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fanhe governor Chao acted with the people's will in removing him to secure the royal house.

sentences.zh: 凡我士庶，同茲休慶！」

translations.literal: All you gentlemen and commoners, share in this blessed rejoicing!"
translations.idiomatic: Let all officers and people share this good fortune!"

sentences.zh: 纂叔父巴西公佗、弟隴西公緯皆在北城。

translations.literal: Zuan's uncle, Duke of Baxi Tuo, and his younger brother, Duke of Longxi Wei, were both in the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's uncle Duke Tuo of Baxi and his brother Duke Wei of Longxi were both in the northern city.

sentences.zh: 或說緯曰：「超為逆亂，公以介弟之親，仗大義而討之。

translations.literal: Someone urged Wei, saying: "Chao has committed rebellion; you, as a close younger brother, should rely on great righteousness to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Wei, "Chao has rebelled; as the late king's own brother you should take up righteous arms against him.

sentences.zh: 姜紀、焦辨在南城，楊桓、田誠在東苑，皆吾黨也，何患不濟！」

translations.literal: Jiang Ji and Jiao Bian are in the southern city, Yang Huan and Tian Cheng in the eastern park—all are our party; why fear failure!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji and Jiao Bian hold the south city, Yang Huan and Tian Cheng the east park—they are all ours; how can we fail!"

sentences.zh: 緯嚴兵欲與佗共擊超。

translations.literal: Wei marshaled troops and wished to join Tuo in attacking Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei gathered troops and prepared to join Tuo in striking Chao.

sentences.zh: 佗妻梁氏止之曰：「緯、超俱兄弟之子，何為捨超助緯，自為禍首乎！」

translations.literal: Tuo's wife, Lady Liang, stopped him, saying: "Wei and Chao are both sons of brothers—why abandon Chao to help Wei and make yourself the author of disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's wife Lady Liang restrained him: "Wei and Chao are both your brother's sons—why side with Wei against Chao and bring ruin on yourself!"

sentences.zh: 佗乃謂緯曰：「超舉事已成，據武庫，擁精兵，圖之甚難。

translations.literal: Tuo then said to Wei: "Chao's undertaking has already succeeded; he holds the armory and commands elite troops—to plot against him is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo then told Wei, "Chao has already won; he holds the arsenal and elite troops—moving against him would be very hard.

sentences.zh: 且吾老矣，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Moreover I am old and can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I am old and powerless to act."

sentences.zh: 超弟邈有寵於緯，說緯曰：「纂賊殺兄弟，隆、超順人心而討之，正欲尊立明公耳。

translations.literal: Chao's younger brother Miao, who enjoyed Wei's favor, urged Wei, saying: "The traitor Zuan killed his brothers; Long and Chao followed the people's hearts in punishing him—they mean precisely to exalt and establish Your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's brother Miao, who had Wei's favor, persuaded him: "The villain Zuan murdered his brothers; Long and Chao acted with the people in punishing him—they mean to set you on the throne.

sentences.zh: 方今明公先帝之長子，當主社稷，人無異望，夫復何疑！」

translations.literal: Now Your Excellency is the former emperor's eldest son and ought to rule the altars of soil and grain; the people have no other wish—what further doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the late emperor's eldest son and should rule the realm; no one looks elsewhere—what is there to doubt!"

sentences.zh: 緯信之，乃與隆、超結盟，單馬入城；

translations.literal: Wei believed him, then allied with Long and Chao and entered the city alone on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: Wei believed him, allied with Long and Chao, and rode into the city alone;

sentences.zh: 超執而殺之。

translations.literal: Chao seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chao seized him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 讓位與隆，隆有難色。

translations.literal: He yielded the throne to Long, and Long showed a troubled countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the throne to Long, who looked uneasy.

sentences.zh: 超曰：「今如乘龍上天，豈可中下！」

translations.literal: Chao said: "Now, as when riding a dragon to heaven, how can one stop halfway!"
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "You are mounting a dragon to the sky—how can you turn back halfway!"

sentences.zh: 隆遂即天王位，大赦，改元神鼎。

translations.literal: Long thereupon assumed the title of Heavenly King, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Shending.
translations.idiomatic: Long then took the title Heavenly King, declared a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Shending.

sentences.zh: 尊母衛氏為太后；

translations.literal: He honored his mother, Lady Wei, as Empress Dowager;
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother Lady Wei as empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 妻楊氏為後；

translations.literal: his wife, Lady Yang, as empress;
translations.idiomatic: his wife Lady Yang as empress;

sentences.zh: 以超為都督中外諸軍事、輔國大將軍、錄尚書書事，封安定公；

translations.literal: he appointed Chao Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General Who Supports the State, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffing him as Duke of Anding;
translations.idiomatic: he made Chao commander of all armies, grand general supporting the state, and overseer of the Masters of Writing, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Anding;

sentences.zh: 謚纂曰靈帝。

translations.literal: and gave Zuan the posthumous title Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: and gave Zuan the posthumous name Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 纂後楊氏將出宮，超恐其挾珍寶，命索之。

translations.literal: Zuan's consort Lady Yang was about to leave the palace; Chao, fearing she carried jewels, ordered a search.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan's queen Lady Yang was to leave the palace, Chao, fearing she would take treasure, ordered her searched.

sentences.zh: 楊氏曰：「爾兄弟不義，手刃相屠。

translations.literal: Lady Yang said: "You brothers are unrighteous, cutting each other down with your own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang said, "You brothers are wicked, slaughtering one another with your own blades.

sentences.zh: 我旦夕死人，安用寶為！」

translations.literal: I am a dead woman before long—of what use are jewels!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall die any day—what need have I of gems!"

sentences.zh: 超又問玉璽所在，楊氏曰：「已毀之矣。」

translations.literal: Chao again asked where the jade seal was; Lady Yang said: "It has already been destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Chao asked where the imperial seal was; Lady Yang said, "I have already destroyed it."

sentences.zh: 後有美色，超將納之，謂其父右僕射桓曰：「後若自殺，禍及卿宗！」

translations.literal: The empress was beautiful; Chao was about to take her in marriage and said to her father, Right Vice Director Huan: "If the empress kills herself, disaster will reach your clan!"
translations.idiomatic: The queen was beautiful, and Chao meant to take her; he told her father, Vice Director Huan, "If the empress takes her own life, your whole clan will suffer!"

sentences.zh: 桓以告楊氏。

translations.literal: Huan told Lady Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan relayed this to Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 楊氏曰：「大人賣女與氐以圖富貴，一之謂甚，其可再乎！」

translations.literal: Lady Yang said: "Elder, you sold your daughter to the Di for wealth and rank—once is already too much; how could it be done again!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang said, "Father, you sold your daughter to the Di for riches once—that was already too much; can you do it again!"

sentences.zh: 遂自殺，謚曰穆後。

translations.literal: She then killed herself and was given the posthumous title Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: She took her own life and was posthumously titled Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 桓奔河西王利鹿孤，利鹿孤以為左司馬。

translations.literal: Huan fled to the Prince of Hexi, Lilugu, who appointed him Left Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled to Prince Lilugu of Hexi, who made him left marshal.

sentences.zh: 三月，孫恩北趣海鹽，劉裕隨而拒之，築城於海鹽故治。

translations.literal: In the third month, Sun En pressed north toward Haiyan; Liu Yu followed to oppose him and built a wall at the old seat of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sun En marched north toward Haiyan; Liu Yu pursued to block him and fortified the old Haiyan seat.

sentences.zh: 恩日來攻城，裕屢擊破之，斬其將姚盛。

translations.literal: En came daily to assault the city; Yu repeatedly defeated him and beheaded his general Yao Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: En attacked the city day after day; Yu beat him back again and again and killed his general Yao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少不敵，裕夜偃旗匿眾，明晨開門，使羸疾數人登城。

translations.literal: The troops in the city were few and could not match the enemy; Yu by night lowered the banners and hid his forces, and at dawn opened the gates and had a few sickly men mount the wall.
translations.idiomatic: With too few men in the city to match the rebels, Yu hid his troops and furled the banners by night; at dawn he opened the gates and posted a few sickly men on the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊遙問劉裕所在，曰：「夜已走矣。」

translations.literal: The rebels asked from afar where Liu Yu was; they were told: "He fled in the night."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shouted from afar asking where Liu Yu was; they were told, "He slipped away in the night."

sentences.zh: 賊信之，爭入城。

translations.literal: The rebels believed it and rushed into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels believed it and scrambled into the city.

sentences.zh: 裕奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Yu struck fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu charged out and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 恩知城不可拔，乃進向滬瀆，裕復棄城追之。

translations.literal: En knew the city could not be taken and advanced toward Hudu; Yu again abandoned the city to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city could not be taken, En marched on toward Hudu; Yu again left the city to pursue.

sentences.zh: 海鹽令鮑陋遣子嗣之帥吳兵一千，請為前驅。

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Haiyan, Bao Lou, sent his son Sizhi to lead a thousand Wu troops and asked to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Lou, magistrate of Haiyan, sent his son Sizhi at the head of a thousand Wu troops and offered to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「賊兵甚精，吳人不習戰，若前驅失利，必敗我軍；

translations.literal: Yu said: "The rebel troops are very skilled; the men of Wu are not practiced in war—if the vanguard is defeated, our army will surely be broken;
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The rebels fight well, and Wu men are unused to battle—if the van is beaten, our whole army will fail;

sentences.zh: 可在後為聲勢。」

translations.literal: they can serve in the rear to lend force."
translations.idiomatic: keep them in the rear to lend weight."

sentences.zh: 嗣之不從。

translations.literal: Sizhi would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi refused.

sentences.zh: 裕乃多伏旗鼓，前驅既交，諸伏皆出。

translations.literal: Yu then set many ambushes with flags and drums; once the vanguard engaged, all the ambushes came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yu laid many ambushes with flags and drums; when the van clashed, every ambush rose.

sentences.zh: 裕舉旗鳴鼓，賊以為四面有軍，乃退。

translations.literal: Yu raised flags and beat drums; the rebels thought armies were on every side and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yu raised banners and drums; the rebels thought they were surrounded and fell back.

sentences.zh: 嗣之追之，戰沒。

translations.literal: Sizhi pursued them and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi pursued and was killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 裕且戰且退，所領死傷且盡，至向戰處，令左右脫取死人衣以示閒暇。

translations.literal: Yu fought as he retreated; those he led were nearly all killed or wounded; when he reached the place of the earlier battle he ordered his attendants to strip the dead of their garments to show leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fought as he withdrew until his men were nearly all dead or wounded; at the earlier battlefield he had his attendants strip the dead of clothing to feign ease.

sentences.zh: 賊疑之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The rebels were suspicious and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected a trap and did not press him.

sentences.zh: 裕大呼更戰，賊懼而退，裕乃引歸。

translations.literal: Yu shouted that he would fight again; the rebels, afraid, withdrew, and Yu then led his force back.
translations.idiomatic: Yu shouted for another round; the rebels, frightened, drew off, and Yu brought his men home.

sentences.zh: 河西王利鹿孤伐涼，與涼王隆戰，大破之，徙二千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hexi, Lilugu, attacked Liang, fought King of Liang Long, routed him utterly, and moved more than two thousand households back.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lilugu of Hexi attacked Liang, defeated King Long in battle, and resettled more than two thousand households on his return.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，魏人罷鄴行台，以所統六郡置相州，以庾岳為刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao, the people of Wei abolished the Ye Branch Directorate and from the six commanderies it ruled established Xiang Province, appointing Yu Yue as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao, Wei abolished the Ye regional headquarters, formed Xiang Province from the six commanderies it had governed, and appointed Yu Yue inspector.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸至苑川，以邊芮為長名，王松壽為司馬，公卿、將帥皆降為僚佐偏裨。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui reached Yuanchuan, made Bian Rui chief clerk, Wang Songsou marshal, and reduced all dukes, ministers, and generals to staff officers and subordinate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui reached Yuanchuan, appointed Bian Rui chief clerk and Wang Songsou marshal, and reduced former nobles and generals to staff and junior officers.

sentences.zh: 北涼王業憚沮渠蒙遜勇略，欲遠之；

translations.literal: King of Northern Liang Ye feared Juqu Mengxun's courage and stratagems and wished to keep him at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: King Ye of Northern Liang feared Juqu Mengxun's ability and meant to send him away;

sentences.zh: 蒙遜亦深自晦匿，業以門下侍郎馬權代蒙遜為張掖太守。

translations.literal: Mengxun also deeply concealed himself; Ye replaced Mengxun as Administrator of Zhangye with Gentleman Attendant of the Household Ma Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun likewise kept a low profile, and Ye replaced him as Zhangye governor with household attendant Ma Quan.

sentences.zh: 權素豪雋，為業所親重，常輕侮蒙遜。

translations.literal: Quan had always been bold and outstanding, was close to and favored by Ye, and often treated Mengxun with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was proud and able, close to Ye, and often slighted Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜譖之於業曰：「天下不足慮，惟當憂馬權耳。」

translations.literal: Mengxun slandered him to Ye, saying: "The realm is not worth worrying over; one need only fear Ma Quan."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun denounced him to Ye, saying, "The realm is no worry—only Ma Quan should concern you."

sentences.zh: 業遂殺權。

translations.literal: Ye thereupon killed Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye then had Quan executed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜謂沮渠男成曰：「段公無鑒斷之才，非撥亂之主，向所憚者惟索嗣、馬權。

translations.literal: Mengxun said to Juqu Nancheng: "Lord Duan lacks the talent for judgment and discernment and is not a ruler who can quell disorder; those we formerly feared were only Suo Si and Ma Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun told Juqu Nancheng, "Lord Duan cannot judge men and is no ruler for troubled times; the only men we feared were Suo Si and Ma Quan.

sentences.zh: 今皆已死，蒙遜欲降之以奉兄，何如？」

translations.literal: Now they are all dead; Mengxun wishes to submit to him to support you, my elder brother—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: They are all dead now. Mengxun wants to win him over to put you, brother, on the throne—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 男成曰：「業本孤客，為吾家所立，恃吾兄弟，猶魚之有水。

translations.literal: Nancheng said: "Ye was originally a lone guest whom our house set up; he relied on us brothers, like a fish that has water.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng said, "Ye was a stranger our clan raised up; he depended on us brothers as fish depend on water.

sentences.zh: 夫人親信我而圖之，不祥。

translations.literal: For a man to plot against one who trusts and favors him is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: To plot against a man who trusts you is ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃求為西安太守。

translations.literal: Mengxun then asked to be made Administrator of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun then requested the post of Xi'an governor.

sentences.zh: 業喜其出外，許之。

translations.literal: Ye was pleased that he would go outside and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was glad to see him leave and agreed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜與男成約同祭蘭門山，而陰使司馬許鹹告業曰：「男成欲以取假日為亂。

translations.literal: Mengxun agreed with Nancheng to sacrifice together at Mount Lanmen, but secretly sent Marshal Xu Xian to tell Ye: "Nancheng means to use the day of rest as a pretext for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun arranged with Nancheng to worship together at Mount Lanmen, but secretly had Marshal Xu Xian tell Ye, "Nancheng plans to rebel on a holiday.

sentences.zh: 若求祭蘭門山，臣言驗矣。」

translations.literal: If he asks to sacrifice at Mount Lanmen, my words will be verified."
translations.idiomatic: If he asks to worship at Mount Lanmen, you will know I speak truth."

sentences.zh: 至期，果然。

translations.literal: When the day came, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, it happened just as he said.

sentences.zh: 業收男成，賜死。

translations.literal: Ye arrested Nancheng and granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: Ye seized Nancheng and ordered him to die.

sentences.zh: 男成曰：「蒙遜先與臣謀反，臣以兄弟之故。

translations.literal: Nancheng said: "Mengxun first plotted rebellion with me; because of our brotherhood I
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng said, "Mengxun first plotted rebellion with me; for our brotherhood's sake I

sentences.zh: 隱而不言。

translations.literal: concealed it and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: kept silent.

sentences.zh: 今以臣在，恐部眾不從，故約臣祭山而返誣臣，其意欲王之殺臣也。

translations.literal: Now, because I remain, he fears the troops will not follow him; therefore he arranged for me to sacrifice on the mountain and then returned to slander me—his intent is that Your Majesty kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with me still alive, he fears the men will not follow him, so he set this mountain rite and then slandered me—he means for Your Majesty to kill me.

sentences.zh: 乞詐言臣死，暴臣罪惡，蒙遜必反；

translations.literal: I beg that you falsely announce my death and expose my crimes; Mengxun will surely rebel;
translations.idiomatic: Pretend I am dead and publish my crimes—Mengxun will surely rebel;

sentences.zh: 臣然後奉王命而討之，無不克矣。」

translations.literal: I will then obey Your Majesty's command to punish him, and success is assured."
translations.idiomatic: then I will strike him under your command and be sure to prevail."

sentences.zh: 業不聽，殺之。

translations.literal: Ye would not listen and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye refused and executed him.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜泣告眾曰：「男成忠於段王，而段王無故枉殺之，諸君能為報仇乎？

translations.literal: Mengxun wept and told the multitude: "Nancheng was loyal to Lord Duan, yet Lord Duan killed him without cause—can you gentlemen avenge him?
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun wept before the troops: "Nancheng was loyal to Lord Duan, yet Duan killed him without cause—will you avenge him?

sentences.zh: 且始者共立段王，欲以安眾耳，今州土紛亂，非段王所能濟也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning we together set up Lord Duan only to settle the multitude; now the province is in turmoil, and Lord Duan cannot save it."
translations.idiomatic: We raised Lord Duan only to calm the people; now the land is in chaos and he cannot save it."

sentences.zh: 男成素得眾心，眾皆憤泣爭奮，比至氐池，眾逾一萬。

translations.literal: Nancheng had long won the people's hearts; all wept in anger and strove to advance; by the time they reached Dichi the host exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng had always held the men's loyalty; they wept in rage and rushed to follow, and by Dichi the host passed ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍臧莫孩帥所部降之，羌、胡多起兵應蒙遜者。

translations.literal: Pacifying-Army General Zang Mohai led his command in surrender; many Qiang and Hu rose in arms to join Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-Army General Zang Mohai surrendered with his troops, and many Qiang and Hu took arms for Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜進壁侯塢。

translations.literal: Mengxun advanced and fortified at Houwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched and encamped at Houwu.

sentences.zh: 業先疑右將軍田昂，囚之；

translations.literal: Ye had earlier suspected Right General Tian Ang and imprisoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Ye had long suspected Right General Tian Ang and held him prisoner;

sentences.zh: 至是召昂，謝而赦之，使與武衛將軍梁中庸共討蒙遜。

translations.literal: now he summoned Ang, apologized and pardoned him, and had him join Martial-Guard General Liang Zhongyong in attacking Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: now he released Ang with an apology and sent him with Martial-Guard General Liang Zhongyong against Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 別將王豐孫言於業曰：「西平諸田，世有反者。

translations.literal: Separate commander Wang Fengsun said to Ye: "The Tian clan of Xiping have produced rebels in every generation.
translations.idiomatic: Separate commander Wang Fengsun told Ye, "The Tian of Xiping rebel in every generation.

sentences.zh: 昂貌恭而心險，不可信也。」

translations.literal: Ang's bearing is respectful but his heart treacherous—he cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Ang looks humble but is treacherous—do not trust him."

sentences.zh: 業曰：「吾疑之久矣，但非昂無可以討蒙遜者。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "I have long suspected him, but apart from Ang there is no one who can attack Mengxun."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "I have doubted him for years, yet no one but Ang can fight Mengxun."

sentences.zh: 昂至侯塢，帥騎五百降於蒙遜，業軍遂潰，中庸亦詣蒙遜降。

translations.literal: When Ang reached Houwu he led five hundred horsemen in surrender to Mengxun; Ye's army then collapsed, and Zhongyong also went to Mengxun and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Houwu Ang surrendered with five hundred horsemen; Ye's army broke, and Zhongyong submitted to Mengxun as well.

sentences.zh: 五月，蒙遜至張掖，田昂兄子承愛斬關內之，業左右皆散。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Mengxun reached Zhangye; Tian Ang's nephew's son Cheng Ai cut down those within the pass, and all around Ye scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Mengxun reached Zhangye; Cheng Ai, nephew of Tian Ang, seized the inner gate, and Ye's attendants fled.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜至，業謂蒙遜曰：「孤孑然一己，為君家所推，願丐餘命，使得東還與妻子相見。」

translations.literal: When Mengxun arrived, Ye said to him: "I stand alone; your house raised me up—I beg a remnant of life so I may go east and see my wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: When Mengxun came, Ye said, "I am alone; your clan set me up—spare my life so I may go east to my wife and children."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜斬之。

translations.literal: Mengxun beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 業，儒素長者，無他權略，威禁不行，群下擅命；

translations.literal: Ye was a plain scholar and elder, without other stratagems; his authority and prohibitions did not prevail, and subordinates acted on their own orders;
translations.idiomatic: Ye was a plain scholar and worthy elder, without craft; his authority did not hold and his officers did as they pleased;

sentences.zh: 尤信卜筮、巫覡，故至於敗。

translations.literal: he especially trusted divination and shamans, and therefore came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: he trusted diviners and shamans above all, and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 沮渠男成之弟富占、將軍俱儽帥戶五百降於河西王利鹿孤。

translations.literal: Juqu Nancheng's younger brother Fuzhan and General Ju Yi led five hundred households in surrender to the Prince of Hexi, Lilugu.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhan, brother of Juqu Nancheng, and General Ju Yi surrendered with five hundred households to Prince Lilugu of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 儽，石子之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Shizi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a son of Shizi.

sentences.zh: 孫恩陷滬瀆，殺吳國內史袁崧，死者四千人。

translations.literal: Sun En took Hudu and killed Interior Minister of Wu Yuan Song; four thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En captured Hudu and killed Yuan Song, interior minister of Wu; four thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 涼王隆多殺豪望以立威名，內外囂然。

translations.literal: King of Liang Long killed many eminent men to establish a fearsome name, and within and without there was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: King Long of Liang killed many leading families to build a fearsome name, and the realm was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 人不自保。

translations.literal: No one could protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: No one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 魏安人焦朗遣使說秦隴西公碩德曰：「呂氏自武皇棄世，兄弟相攻，政綱不立，競為威虐。

translations.literal: Jiao Lang of Wei'an sent an envoy to persuade the Duke of Longxi of Qin, Shide, saying: "Since the Martial Emperor of the Lü clan left the world, brothers have attacked one another; government laws are not established, and all compete in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lang of Wei'an sent envoys to Duke Shide of Longxi in Qin, saying, "Since the Lü Martial Emperor died, his sons have fought one another; law has collapsed and all vie in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 百姓饑饉，死者過半。

translations.literal: The common people suffer famine; more than half have died.
translations.idiomatic: The people starve; more than half are dead.

sentences.zh: 今乘其纂奪之際，取之易於返掌，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Now, seizing the moment of usurpation and seizure, to take it is easier than turning the hand—this must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Strike now, while they usurp and seize—it is easier than turning your hand; do not miss it."

sentences.zh: 碩德言於秦王興，帥步騎六萬伐涼，乞伏乾歸帥騎七千從之。

translations.literal: Shide spoke to King of Qin Yao Xing, who led sixty thousand foot and horse to attack Liang; Qifu Gangui led seven thousand horse in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Shide persuaded King Yao Xing of Qin, who marched sixty thousand foot and horse against Liang, with Qifu Gangui and seven thousand cavalry in support.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，孫恩浮海奄至丹徒，戰士十餘萬，樓船千餘艘，建康震駭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, Sun En came by sea and suddenly reached Dantu with more than a hundred thousand warriors and over a thousand tower ships; Jiankang was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, Sun En came by sea to Dantu with more than a hundred thousand fighters and a thousand warships, and Jiankang was terrified.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，內外戒嚴，百官入居省內。

translations.literal: On yihai, inner and outer defenses were placed on alert and all officials entered and lodged within the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the capital was placed under martial law and officials moved into the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍高素等守石頭，輔國將軍劉襲柵斷淮口，丹陽尹司馬恢之戍南岸，冠軍將軍桓謙等備白石，左衛將軍王嘏等屯中堂，征豫州刺史譙王尚之入衛京師。

translations.literal: Champion General Gao Su and others guarded Stone City; General Who Supports the State Liu Xi barred the Huai mouth with palisades; Administrator of Danyang Sima Huizhi garrisoned the south bank; Champion General Huan Qian and others prepared at Baishi; Left Guard General Wang Jia and others encamped at Zhongtang; the campaign Inspector of Yuzhou, Prince of Qiao Shangzhi, entered to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Gao Su held Stone City; Liu Xi of the supporting state barred the Huai; Danyang governor Sima Huizhi held the south bank; Huan Qian prepared at Baishi; Wang Jia camped at Zhongtang; and Prince Shangzhi of Qiao marched in from Yuzhou to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之自山陰引兵邀擊恩，未至而恩已過，乃使劉裕自海鹽入援。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi led troops from Shanyin to intercept En but did not arrive before En had passed; he then sent Liu Yu from Haiyan as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi marched from Shanyin to cut En off but arrived too late and sent Liu Yu from Haiyan to reinforce the capital.

sentences.zh: 裕兵不滿千人，倍道兼行，與恩俱至丹徒。

translations.literal: Yu's troops were fewer than a thousand; he marched by double stages day and night and reached Dantu together with En.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had fewer than a thousand men and forced the march day and night, reaching Dantu as En did.

sentences.zh: 裕眾既少，加以涉遠疲勞，而丹徒守軍莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: Yu's host was already few, and in addition they were worn from the long march; the garrison at Dantu had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was badly outnumbered and his men were exhausted from the long march, while the Dantu garrison had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 恩帥眾鼓噪，登蒜山，居民皆荷擔而立。

translations.literal: En led his host with drums and shouts, climbed Garlic Mountain, and the inhabitants all stood with packs on their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: En led his men with drums and shouts up Garlic Mountain, and the townspeople stood ready with bundles on their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 裕帥所領奔擊，大破之，投崖赴水死者甚眾，恩狼狽僅得還船。

translations.literal: Yu led those he commanded in a rushing attack and routed them utterly; many who threw themselves from cliffs or into the water died; En in disgrace barely got back to his ships.
translations.idiomatic: Yu charged and smashed them; many leapt from cliffs or drowned, and En barely escaped back to his ships.

sentences.zh: 然恩猶恃其眾，尋復整兵徑向京師。

translations.literal: Yet En still relied on his numbers and soon regrouped his troops and headed straight for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yet En still trusted his numbers, regrouped, and marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 後將軍元顯帥兵拒戰，頻不利。

translations.literal: Rear General Yuan Xian led troops to resist but met repeated setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Yuan Xian met him in battle but lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子無他謀略，唯日禱蔣侯廟。

translations.literal: Dao Zi, Prince of Kuaiji, had no other stratagem and only prayed daily at the temple of Marquis Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao Zi of Kuaiji had no plan but daily prayers at the temple of Marquis Jiang.

sentences.zh: 恩來漸近，百姓恟懼。

translations.literal: As En drew gradually nearer, the people were alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: As En drew near, the people panicked.

sentences.zh: 譙王尚之帥精銳馳至，逕屯積弩堂。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao Shangzhi led elite troops at full gallop and went straight to encamp at the Hall of Accumulated Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shangzhi of Qiao raced up with picked troops and camped at the Hall of Accumulated Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 恩樓船高大，溯風不得疾行，數日乃至白石。

translations.literal: En's tower ships were tall and large; against the wind they could not sail swiftly, and only after several days did they reach Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: En's tall warships could not make speed against the wind and took days to reach Baishi.

sentences.zh: 恩本以諸軍分散，欲掩不備；

translations.literal: En had originally thought the armies were scattered and wished to strike them unprepared;
translations.idiomatic: En had hoped the imperial forces were scattered and meant to strike by surprise;

sentences.zh: 既而知尚之在建康，復聞劉牢之已還，至新洲，不敢進而去，浮海北走郁洲。

translations.literal: when he learned that Shangzhi was in Jiankang and again heard that Liu Laozhi had returned, he reached Xinzhou, did not dare advance but withdrew, and fled north by sea to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: but learning Shangzhi was in Jiankang and Liu Laozhi had returned, he halted at Xinzhou, dared not advance, and fled north by sea to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 恩別將攻陷廣陵，殺三千人。

translations.literal: En's separate commander attacked and took Guangling and killed three thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: A detached force under En took Guangling and killed three thousand.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍高雅之擊恩於郁洲，為恩所執。

translations.literal: Pacifying-North General Gao Yazhi attacked En at Yuzhou and was seized by En.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-North General Gao Yazhi attacked En at Yuzhou and was captured.

sentences.zh: 桓玄厲兵訓卒，常伺朝廷之隙，聞孫恩逼京師，建牙聚眾，上疏請討之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan drilled troops and trained soldiers, always watching for openings in the court; hearing that Sun En pressed on the capital, he raised his standard and gathered hosts and submitted a memorial asking to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan kept his army sharp and watched for court weakness; when Sun En threatened the capital he mobilized and memorialized for permission to attack.

sentences.zh: 元顯大懼。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian was terrified.

sentences.zh: 會恩退，元顯以詔書止之，玄乃解嚴。

translations.literal: When En withdrew, Yuan Xian used an imperial edict to stop him, and Xuan then stood down from alert.
translations.idiomatic: When En withdrew, Yuan Xian used an edict to stop him, and Huan stood his troops down.

sentences.zh: 梁中庸等共推沮渠蒙遜為大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、張掖公，赦其境內，改元永安。

translations.literal: Liang Zhongyong and others together acclaimed Juqu Mengxun as Grand Commander, Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Zhangye; he pardoned those within his borders and changed the era name to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhongyong and others made Juqu Mengxun grand commander, grand general, Governor of Liang, and Duke of Zhangye; he pardoned his realm and adopted the era name Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜署從兄伏奴為張掖太守、和平侯，弟挐為建忠將軍、都谷侯，田昂為西郡太守，臧莫孩為輔國將軍，房晷、梁中庸為左、右長史，張騭、謝正禮為左右司馬。

translations.literal: Mengxun appointed his father's brother's son Funu Administrator of Zhangye and Marquis of Heping, his younger brother Na General Who Establishes Loyalty and Marquis of Dugu, Tian Ang Administrator of Xijun, Zang Mohai General Who Supports the State, Fang Gui and Liang Zhongyong left and right chief clerks, and Zhang Yi and Xie Zhengli left and right marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun made his cousin Funu Zhangye governor and Marquis of Heping, his brother Na general establishing loyalty and Marquis of Dugu, Tian Ang Xijun governor, Zang Mohai supporting-state general, Fang Gui and Liang Zhongyong chief clerks, and Zhang Yi and Xie Zhengli marshals.

sentences.zh: 擢任賢才，文武鹹悅。

translations.literal: He promoted and employed worthy talent; civil and military alike were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He raised able men, and civil and military officers alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 河西王利鹿孤命群臣極言得失。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hexi, Lilugu, ordered his ministers to speak to the utmost on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lilugu of Hexi ordered his ministers to speak freely of the state's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 西曹從事史暠曰：「陛下命將出征，往無不捷。

translations.literal: Western Bureau Attendant Shi Gao said: "Your Majesty sends generals on campaign, and in the past none have failed to win.
translations.idiomatic: Western Bureau attendant Shi Gao said, "Your Majesty sends generals to war and they have never failed.

sentences.zh: 然不以綏寧為先，唯以徙民為務；

translations.literal: Yet you do not put pacification first and only make relocating the people your task;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you put relocation ahead of pacification;

sentences.zh: 民安土重遷，故多離叛，此所以斬將拔城而地不加廣也。」

translations.literal: the people love their native soil and dread moving, so many desert—this is why you cut down generals and take cities yet your territory does not grow wider."
translations.idiomatic: people cling to their homes and flee resettlement, so though you win battles and take cities your domain does not grow."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤善之。

translations.literal: Lilugu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏兗州刺史長孫肥將步騎二萬南徇許昌，東至彭城，將軍劉該降之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yu Yue, Inspector of Yan Province of Wei, Changsun Fei led twenty thousand foot and horse south to overrun Xuchang and east to Pengcheng; General Liu Gai surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Changsun Fei, Yan inspector of Wei, led twenty thousand foot and horse south against Xuchang and east to Pengcheng; General Liu Gai surrendered.

sentences.zh: 秦隴西公碩德自金城濟河，直趣廣武，河西王利鹿孤攝廣武守軍避之。

translations.literal: The Duke of Longxi of Qin, Shide, crossed the river from Jincheng and went straight for Guangwu; the Prince of Hexi, Lilugu, gathered the Guangwu garrison and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shide of Longxi in Qin crossed from Jincheng and marched on Guangwu; Prince Lilugu of Hexi withdrew the Guangwu garrison.

sentences.zh: 秦軍至姑臧，涼王隆遣輔國大將軍超、龍驤將軍邈等逆戰，碩德大破之，生擒邈，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: When the Qin army reached Guzang, King of Liang Long sent General Who Supports the State Chao, Dragon-Prancing General Miao, and others to meet them in battle; Shide routed them utterly, captured Miao alive, and took or killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang King Long of Liang sent Chao, supporting-state grand general, and Miao, dragon-prancing general, against them; Shide crushed the army, took Miao alive, and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 隆嬰城固守，巴西公佗帥東苑之眾二萬五千降於秦。

translations.literal: Long shut the city and held firm; Duke of Baxi Tuo led twenty-five thousand of the eastern park troops in surrender to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Long shut himself in the city; Duke Tuo of Baxi surrendered with twenty-five thousand men from the eastern park.

sentences.zh: 西涼公暠、河西王利鹿孤、沮渠蒙遜各遣使奉表入貢於秦。

translations.literal: The Duke of Western Liang, Gao, the Prince of Hexi, Lilugu, and Juqu Mengxun each sent envoys bearing memorials to offer tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Gao of Western Liang, Prince Lilugu of Hexi, and Juqu Mengxun each sent tribute missions to Qin.

sentences.zh: 初，涼將姜紀降於河西王利鹿孤，廣武公辱檀與論兵略，甚愛重之，坐則連席，出則同車，每談論，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Liang general Jiang Ji had surrendered to the Prince of Hexi, Lilugu; Duke of Guangwu Rutan discussed military strategy with him and greatly loved and valued him—they sat with joined mats and went out in the same carriage, and whenever they talked, night followed day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Liang general Jiang Ji had surrendered to Prince Lilugu of Hexi; Duke Rutan of Guangwu delighted in his military talk, shared mat and carriage with him, and their discussions ran night into day.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤謂辱檀曰：「姜紀信有美才，然視候非常，必不久留於此，不如殺之。

translations.literal: Lilugu said to Rutan: "Jiang Ji truly has fine talent, yet his gaze and bearing are extraordinary; he will surely not long remain here—better to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu told Rutan, "Jiang Ji is able, but his manner is strange and he will not stay—better kill him.

sentences.zh: 紀若入秦，必為人患。」

translations.literal: If Ji enters Qin he will surely become a trouble to men."
translations.idiomatic: If he goes to Qin he will become a danger."

sentences.zh: 辱檀曰：「臣以布衣之交待紀，紀必不相負也。」

translations.literal: Rutan said: "I treat Ji with the friendship of plain cloth; Ji will surely not fail me."
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "I have treated him as a friend of the road; he will not betray me."

sentences.zh: 八月，紀將數十騎奔秦軍，說碩德曰：「呂隆孤城無援，明公以大軍臨之，其勢必請降；

translations.literal: In the eighth month Ji led several tens of horsemen in flight to the Qin army and said to Shide: "Lü Long is a lone city without aid; when Your Excellency brings a great army against it, the situation will surely make him beg to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ji fled with a few dozen horsemen to the Qin army and told Shide, "Lü Long holds a lone city; your great army will force him to sue for peace;

sentences.zh: 然彼徙文降而已，未肯遂服也。

translations.literal: yet he will only remove the text of submission and surrender on paper and will not be willing to submit in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: but that will be a paper surrender, not true submission.

sentences.zh: 請給紀步騎三千，與王松匆因焦朗、華純之眾，伺其釁隙，隆不足取也。

translations.literal: I beg you give Ji three thousand foot and horse; with Wang Songcong, relying on the hosts of Jiao Lang and Hua Chunzhi, we will watch for an opening—Long is not hard to take.
translations.idiomatic: Give me three thousand foot and horse with Wang Songcong, Jiao Lang, and Hua Chunzhi—we will watch for a chance, and Long will be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 不然，今禿髮在南，兵強國富，若兼姑臧而據之，威勢益盛，沮渠蒙遜、李暠不能抗也，必將歸之，如此，則為國家之大敵矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, now the Tufa are in the south, strong in troops and rich in state; if they take Guzang as well and hold it, their power and prestige will grow still greater, and Juqu Mengxun and Li Gao cannot resist—they will surely submit to them; thus they will become a great enemy of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the Tufa in the south are strong and rich; if they take Guzang their power will grow, Mengxun and Li Gao cannot stand against them, and they will submit—then you will have a great enemy."

sentences.zh: 碩德乃表紀為武威太守。

translations.literal: Shide then memorialized to make Ji Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shide then recommended Ji as Wuwei governor.

sentences.zh: 配兵二千，屯據晏然。

translations.literal: He assigned him two thousand troops to garrison and hold Yanran.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him two thousand men and posted him at Yanran.

sentences.zh: 秦王興聞楊桓之賢而征之，利鹿孤不敢留。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin heard of Yang Huan's worth and summoned him; Lilugu did not dare detain him.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xing of Qin heard of Yang Huan's excellence he summoned him, and Lilugu did not dare keep him.

sentences.zh: 詔以劉裕下邳太守，討孫恩於郁洲，累戰，大破之。

translations.literal: An edict made Liu Yu Administrator of Xiapi to attack Sun En at Yuzhou; after repeated battles he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order appointed Liu Yu governor of Xiapi and sent him against Sun En at Yuzhou; after several engagements he won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 恩由是衰弱，復緣海南走，裕亦隨而邀擊之。

translations.literal: En thereby weakened, again fled south along the sea, and Yu also followed and intercepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En grew weaker and fled south along the coast again; Liu Yu pursued and struck at him.

sentences.zh: 燕王盛懲其父寶以懦弱失國，務峻威刑，又自矜聰察，多所猜忌，群臣有纖介之嫌，皆先事誅之。

translations.literal: King Sheng of Yan, taking warning from his father Bao's loss of the state through weakness, devoted himself to harsh penalties; he also prided himself on keen perception, was much suspicious, and if any minister bore the slightest taint he put them to death beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: King Sheng of Yan, mindful that his father Bao had lost the realm through timidity, relied on harsh punishments. He prided himself on his sharp judgment, suspected everyone, and executed any minister against whom the faintest suspicion arose—before trouble could even break out.

sentences.zh: 由是宗親、勳舊，人不自保。

translations.literal: Thereby among kinsmen and meritorious elders, no one could keep himself safe.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whether kinsman or old companion of the throne, no one could feel secure.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，左將軍慕容國與殿上將軍秦輿、段贊謀帥禁兵襲盛，事發，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Left General Murong Guo with Palace Guard General Qin Yu and Duan Zan plotted to lead the forbidden troops in a surprise attack on Sheng; the matter was exposed, and more than five hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Left General Murong Guo, Palace Guard General Qin Yu, and Duan Zan plotted to lead the palace guard against Sheng. The conspiracy was discovered, and more than five hundred people were killed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰夜，前將軍段璣與秦輿之子興、段贊之子泰潛於禁中鼓噪大呼。

translations.literal: On the night of renchen, former General Duan Ji with Qin Yu's son Xing and Duan Zan's son Tai secretly entered the inner palace, beat drums, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on renchen, former General Duan Ji, Qin Yu's son Xing, and Duan Zan's son Tai slipped into the inner palace, raised a clamor of drums and shouting.

sentences.zh: 盛聞變，帥左右出戰，賊眾逃潰。

translations.literal: Sheng heard of the disturbance, led his personal guard out to fight, and the rebel host fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng heard the uproar, took his personal guard out to fight, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 璣被創，匿廂屋間。

translations.literal: Ji was wounded and hid between the side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was wounded and hid in the side chambers.

sentences.zh: 俄有一賊從暗中擊盛，盛被傷，輦升前殿，申約禁衛，事寧而卒。

translations.literal: Before long a rebel struck Sheng from hiding; Sheng was wounded, was borne up to the front hall, tightened the forbidden guards' discipline, and when the affair was settled he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a rebel struck Sheng from the shadows. Wounded, he was carried to the front hall, tightened discipline among the guards, and died once order was restored.

sentences.zh: 中壘將軍慕容拔、冗從僕射郭仲白太后丁氏，以為國家多難，宜立長君。

translations.literal: Central Rampart General Murong Ba and Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Zhong told Empress Dowager Lady Ding that with many difficulties besetting the state they ought to establish an elder lord.
translations.idiomatic: Central Rampart General Murong Ba and Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Zhong told Empress Dowager Ding that the realm was in crisis and needed an elder, seasoned ruler.

sentences.zh: 時眾望在盛弟司徒、尚書令、平原公元，而河間公熙素得幸於丁氏，丁氏乃廢太子定，密迎熙入宮。

translations.literal: At the time popular hope rested on Sheng's younger brother the Minister over the Masses, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince Yuan of Pingyuan; but Prince Xi of Hejian had long won Lady Ding's favor, and Lady Ding thereupon deposed Crown Prince Ding and secretly welcomed Xi into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Popular expectation favored Sheng's younger brother Yuan, Prince of Pingyuan, who held the posts of Minister over the Masses and Director of the Imperial Secretariat. But Prince Xi of Hejian had long enjoyed Lady Ding's favor, so she deposed Crown Prince Ding and secretly brought Xi into the palace.

sentences.zh: 明旦，群臣入朝，始知有變，因上表勸進於熙。

translations.literal: At dawn the ministers entered court, only then learned of the change, and accordingly submitted a memorial urging Xi to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the ministers came to court, learned of the coup for the first time, and submitted memorials urging Xi to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 熙以讓元，元不敢當。

translations.literal: Xi yielded to Yuan; Yuan did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xi offered the throne to Yuan, but Yuan dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，熙即天王位，捕獲段璣等，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: On guisi Xi assumed the title of Heavenly King; Duan Ji and the others were captured and all their three clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Xi took the throne as Heavenly King. Duan Ji and his fellows were captured, and their clans were exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 甲午，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiawu a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，平原公元以嫌賜死。

translations.literal: On bingshen Prince Yuan of Pingyuan was ordered to die on account of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Prince Yuan of Pingyuan was forced to take his own life on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 閏月，辛酉，葬盛於興平陵，謚曰昭武皇帝，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinyou, they buried Sheng at Xingping Tomb, posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on xinyou, Sheng was buried at Xingping Tomb with the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu and temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 丁氏送葬未還，中領軍慕容提、步軍校尉張佛等謀立故太子定，事覺，伏誅，定亦賜死。

translations.literal: Before Lady Ding returned from the funeral, Central Army Commander Murong Ti and Infantry Commandant Zhang Fo and others plotted to enthrone the former crown prince Ding; when discovered they were executed, and Ding was also ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lady Ding returned from the funeral, Central Army Commander Murong Ti, Infantry Commandant Zhang Fo, and others plotted to restore the former crown prince Ding. The plot was exposed; they were executed, and Ding was forced to die as well.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，大赦，改元光始。

translations.literal: On bingyin a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin a general amnesty was declared and the reign era was changed to Guangshi.

sentences.zh: 秦隴西公碩德圍姑臧累月，東方之人在城中者多謀外叛，魏益多復誘扇之，欲殺涼王隆及安定公超，事發，坐死者三百餘家。

translations.literal: Qin Prince Shide of Longxi besieged Guzang for many months; many easterners in the city plotted to defect outward, and Wei Yiduo again incited them, intending to kill King Long of Liang and Prince Chao of Anding; when the plot was exposed more than three hundred families were put to death for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Prince Shide of Longxi had besieged Guzang for months. Many easterners inside the city plotted to defect, and Wei Yiduo again stirred them up, planning to kill King Long of Liang and Prince Chao of Anding. When the plot was uncovered, more than three hundred families were executed.

sentences.zh: 碩德撫納夷、夏，分置守宰，節食聚粟。

translations.literal: Shide soothed and received both barbarians and Chinese, appointed guards and magistrates in divisions, economized food and gathered grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shide won over both tribal peoples and Chinese, posted officials throughout the territory, rationed food, and stockpiled grain.

sentences.zh: 為持久之計。

translations.literal: He prepared for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was planning for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 涼之群臣請與秦連和，隆不許。

translations.literal: Liang's ministers asked to ally with Qin; Long would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's ministers urged an alliance with Qin, but Long refused.

sentences.zh: 安守公超曰：「今資儲內竭，上下嗷嗷，雖使張、陳復生，亦無以為策。

translations.literal: Prince Anshou Chao said: "Now stores within are exhausted and above and below cry out in distress; even if Zhang and Chen were revived, there would be no stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chao of Anding said, "Our reserves are spent and the court and people are desperate. Even if Zhang Liang and Chen Ping rose from the dead, they could offer no plan.

sentences.zh: 陛下當思權變屈伸，何愛尺書、單使為卑辭以退敵！

translations.literal: Your Majesty should think of flexible advance and retreat—why cherish a brief letter or a lone envoy and use humble words to repel the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must bend when the times require it. Why cling to pride over a short letter or a single envoy and refuse humble words that could send the enemy away!

sentences.zh: 敵去之後，修德政以息民，若卜世未窮，何憂舊業之不復！

translations.literal: After the enemy departs, cultivate virtuous government to give the people rest; if your allotted span is not yet exhausted, why worry that the old enterprise will not be restored!
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy withdraws, govern well and let the people recover. If Heaven has not ended your line, why fear that your former realm cannot be restored!

sentences.zh: 若天命去矣，亦可以保全宗族。

translations.literal: If the Mandate of Heaven has already departed, you may still preserve the clan.
translations.idiomatic: If the Mandate has truly passed, you may at least preserve your clan.

sentences.zh: 不然，坐守困窮，終將何如！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, sitting in defense of exhaustion—in the end what then!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, to sit here until we are worn down—what end can that have!"

sentences.zh: 隆乃從之，九月，遣使請降於秦。

translations.literal: Long then followed this advice; in the ninth month he sent envoys to beg surrender to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Long accepted his counsel. In the ninth month he sent envoys to surrender to Qin.

sentences.zh: 碩德表隆為鎮西大將軍、涼州刺史、建康公。

translations.literal: Shide memorialized to make Long General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shide recommended Long as General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 隆遣子弟及文武舊臣慕容築、楊穎等五十餘家入質於長安。

translations.literal: Long sent his sons and younger brothers and old civil and military officers Murong Zhu, Yang Ying, and more than fifty families as hostages to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Long sent his sons and brothers, together with veteran officials such as Murong Zhu and Yang Ying—more than fifty households in all—as hostages to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 碩德軍令嚴整，秋毫不犯，祭先賢，禮名士，西土悅之。

translations.literal: Shide's military orders were strict and orderly; he did not violate so much as an autumn hair, sacrificed to former worthies, treated eminent men with courtesy, and the western lands were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shide kept strict discipline and did not harm so much as a blade of grass. He honored past sages and treated eminent men with respect, and the western regions welcomed his rule.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜所部酒泉、涼寧二郡叛降於西涼，又聞呂隆降秦，大懼，遣其弟建忠將軍挐、牧府長史張潛見碩德於姑臧，請帥其眾東遷。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Jiuquan and Liangning under Juqu Mengxun rebelled and surrendered to Western Liang; upon further hearing that Lü Long had surrendered to Qin he was greatly afraid, and sent his younger brother the Establishing Loyalty General Nuo and the Pasturage Office Master of Records Zhang Qian to see Shide at Guzang, asking to lead his masses east in migration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuquan and Liangning, the two prefectures under Juqu Mengxun, rebelled and went over to Western Liang. When he also heard that Lü Long had surrendered to Qin he was terrified and sent his younger brother Nuo, the Establishing Loyalty General, and Zhang Qian, chief clerk of the pasturage office, to see Shide at Guzang and ask permission to lead his people east in migration.

sentences.zh: 碩德喜，拜潛張掖太守，挐建康太守。

translations.literal: Shide was pleased, appointed Qian Administrator of Zhangye and Nuo Administrator of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shide was delighted and appointed Qian governor of Zhangye and Nuo governor of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 潛勸蒙遜東遷。

translations.literal: Qian urged Mengxun to migrate east.
translations.idiomatic: Qian urged Mengxun to move east.

sentences.zh: 挐私謂蒙遜曰：「姑臧未拔，呂氏猶存，碩德糧盡將還，不能久也。

translations.literal: In private Nuo said to Mengxun: "Guzang is not yet taken, the Lü clan still exists; when Shide's grain is exhausted he will return and cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Nuo said privately to Mengxun, "Guzang has not fallen and the Lü are still in power. When Shide runs out of grain he will withdraw and cannot remain long.

sentences.zh: 何為自棄土宇，受制於人乎！」

translations.literal: Why abandon your territory and fall under another's control!"
translations.idiomatic: Why throw away your own lands and submit to someone else's rule!"

sentences.zh: 臧莫孩亦以為然。

translations.literal: Zang Mohai also considered this right.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mohai agreed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣子奚念為質於河西王利鹿孤，利鹿孤不受，曰：「奚念年少，可遣挐也。」

translations.literal: Mengxun sent his son Xinian as hostage to Western River King Lilugu; Lilugu would not accept him, saying: "Xinian is young; you may send Nuo instead."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent his son Xinian as a hostage to Western River King Lilugu. Lilugu refused him, saying, "Xinian is too young. Send Nuo instead."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，蒙遜復遣使上疏於利鹿孤曰：「臣前遣奚念具披誠款，而聖旨未昭，復征弟挐。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Mengxun again sent envoys with a memorial upward to Lilugu saying: "Your servant previously sent Xinian fully to lay forth sincere allegiance, yet Your Sage's intention was not made clear and you again summon my younger brother Nuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Mengxun again sent a memorial to Lilugu: "Your servant earlier sent Xinian to lay my loyalty fully before you, yet your will was unclear and you now demand my younger brother Nuo as well.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為苟有誠信，則子不為輕；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that if there is sincerity and trust, then a son is not light;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that where there is sincerity and trust, a son is pledge enough;

sentences.zh: 若其不信，則弟不為重。

translations.literal: if there is no trust, then a younger brother is not weighty.
translations.idiomatic: and where there is no trust, a younger brother counts for nothing.

sentences.zh: 今寇難未夷，不獲奉詔，願陛下亮之。」

translations.literal: Now bandit difficulties are not yet quelled and I cannot follow the edict; I beg Your Majesty to understand this."
translations.idiomatic: Bandit troubles are not yet settled and I cannot obey your command. I beg Your Majesty to understand."

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤怒，遣張松侯俱延、興城侯文支將騎一萬襲蒙遜，至萬歲臨松，執蒙遜從弟鄯善苟子，虜其民六千餘戶。

translations.literal: Lilugu was enraged and sent Zhang, Marquis of Song, Juyan, and Marquis of Xingcheng, Wenzhi, leading ten thousand cavalry to strike Mengxun; reaching Wansui Lin song, they seized Mengxun's younger cousin Shanshan Gouzi and captured more than six thousand households of his people.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu was furious. He sent Juyan, Marquis of Song, and Wenzhi, Marquis of Xingcheng, with ten thousand horsemen against Mengxun. At Wansui Lin song they seized Mengxun's cousin Gouzi of Shanshan and carried off more than six thousand of his households.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜從叔孔遮入朝於利鹿孤，許以挐為質。

translations.literal: Mengxun's uncle by the father's side Kong Zhe entered court to Lilugu and promised to give Nuo as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun's uncle Kong Zhe came to Lilugu's court and promised to send Nuo as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤乃歸其所掠，召俱延等還。

translations.literal: Lilugu then returned what they had seized and summoned Juyan and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu then returned the captives and recalled Juyan and his force.

sentences.zh: 文支，利鹿孤之弟也。

translations.literal: Wenzhi was Lilugu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi was Lilugu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 南燕主備德宴群臣於延賢堂，酒酣，謂君臣曰：「朕可方自古何等主？」

translations.literal: Southern Yan ruler Beide feasted the ministers at the Hall for Advancing the Worthy; when the wine was deep he said to lord and minister: "How may I be compared to which lord of antiquity?"
translations.idiomatic: Beide, ruler of Southern Yan, feasted his ministers in the Hall for Advancing the Worthy. When the wine had gone deep he asked them, "To which ruler of old may I be compared?"

sentences.zh: 青州刺史鞠仲曰：「陛下中興聖主，少康、光武之儔。」

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Qingzhou Ju Zhong said: "Your Majesty is a sage who restored the realm, the peer of Shaokang and Guangwu."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou inspector Ju Zhong said, "Your Majesty is a sage who restored the realm—the equal of Shaokang and Emperor Guangwu."

sentences.zh: 備德顧左右賜仲帛千匹，仲以所賜多，辭之。

translations.literal: Beide looked to those at his side and rewarded Zhong with a thousand bolts of silk; Zhong, because the gift was large, declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Beide turned to his attendants and had a thousand bolts of silk given to Zhong. Zhong declined, saying the reward was too great.

sentences.zh: 備德曰：「卿知調朕，朕不知調卿邪！

translations.literal: Beide said: "You know how to flatter me—do I not know how to flatter you!
translations.idiomatic: Beide said, "You know how to flatter me—do you think I do not know how to flatter you in return!

sentences.zh: 卿所以非實，故朕亦以虛言賞卿耳。」

translations.literal: Because your words were unreal, I also reward you with unreal words."
translations.idiomatic: Because your praise was empty, I reward you with empty words as well."

sentences.zh: 韓范進曰：「天子無戲言。

translations.literal: Han Fan advanced and said: "The Son of Heaven has no jesting words.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan stepped forward and said, "A Son of Heaven does not speak in jest.

sentences.zh: 今日之論，君臣俱失。」

translations.literal: In today's discussion, lord and minister both erred."
translations.idiomatic: In today's exchange, both ruler and subject were at fault."

sentences.zh: 備德大悅，賜范絹五十匹。

translations.literal: Beide was greatly pleased and bestowed on Fan fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Beide was delighted and gave Fan fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 備德母及兄納皆在長安，備德遣平原人杜弘往訪之。

translations.literal: Beide's mother and elder brother Na were both in Chang'an; Beide sent Du Hong of Pingyuan to visit them.
translations.idiomatic: Beide's mother and elder brother Na were both in Chang'an, so Beide sent Du Hong of Pingyuan to visit them.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「臣至長安，若不奉太后動止，當西如張掖，以死為效。

translations.literal: Hong said: "When your servant reaches Chang'an, if I do not obtain news of the Empress Dowager's wellbeing I shall go west to Zhangye and offer my death in service.
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "When I reach Chang'an, if I cannot learn how the Empress Dowager fares, I shall go west to Zhangye and offer my life in your service.

sentences.zh: 臣父雄年逾六十，乞本縣之祿以申烏鳥之情。」

translations.literal: My father Xiong is over sixty; I beg the salary of my native county to fulfill the feeling of the nesting bird."
translations.idiomatic: My father Xiong is past sixty. I beg a stipend in our home county so I may honor him as a son should."

sentences.zh: 中書令張華曰：「杜弘未行而求祿，要君之罪大矣。」

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Zhang Hua said: "Du Hong has not yet departed and seeks salary—his crime of coercing the ruler is grave."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Zhang Hua said, "Du Hong seeks a salary before he has even set out. That is the grave offense of coercing one's lord."

sentences.zh: 備德曰：「弘為君迎母，為父求祿，忠孝備矣，何罪之有！」

translations.literal: Beide said: "Hong serves his ruler by welcoming his mother and serves his father by seeking salary—filial piety and loyalty are both complete; where is the crime!"
translations.idiomatic: Beide said, "Hong serves his ruler by fetching his mother and serves his father by asking for a stipend. Loyalty and filial piety are both fulfilled—what crime is there!"

sentences.zh: 以雄為平原令。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiong Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiong magistrate of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘至張掖，為盜所殺。

translations.literal: Hong reached Zhangye and was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reached Zhangye and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 十一月，劉裕追孫恩至滬瀆、海鹽，又破之，俘斬以萬數，恩遂自浹口遠竄入海。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Liu Yu pursued Sun En to Hudu and Haiyan and again defeated him; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands, and En thereupon fled far from Jiekou out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Liu Yu pursued Sun En to Hudu and Haiyan and defeated him again. Captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands, and En fled from Jiekou far out to sea.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，魏主珪遣常山王遵、定陵公和跋帥眾五萬襲沒弈干於高平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, Wei Emperor Gui sent Prince Changshan Zun and Duke Dingling Heba leading fifty thousand men to strike Moyigan at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, Wei Emperor Gui sent Prince Changshan Zun and Duke Dingling Heba with fifty thousand men to attack Moyigan at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏虎威將軍宿沓干伐燕，攻令支；

translations.literal: On yimao Wei Tiger Might General Su Daggan attacked Yan and assaulted Lingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Wei's Tiger Might General Su Daggan attacked Yan and besieged Lingzhi;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，燕中領軍宇文拔救之。

translations.literal: on yichou Yan Central Army Commander Murong Ba went to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: on yichou Yan's Central Army Commander Murong Ba marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 壬午，宿沓干拔令支而戍之。

translations.literal: On renchen Su Daggan took Lingzhi and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Su Daggan captured Lingzhi and left a garrison.

sentences.zh: 呂超攻姜紀，不克，遂攻焦朗。

translations.literal: Lü Chao attacked Jiang Ji but could not take him, then attacked Jiao Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao attacked Jiang Ji without success, then turned against Jiao Lang.

sentences.zh: 朗遣其弟子嵩為質於河西王利鹿孤以請迎，利鹿孤遣車騎將軍辱檀赴之。

translations.literal: Lang sent his younger brother's son Song as hostage to Western River King Lilugu to ask for a welcome; Lilugu sent Cavalry General Rutan to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lang sent his nephew Song as a hostage to Western River King Lilugu to ask for relief. Lilugu sent Cavalry General Rutan to his aid.

sentences.zh: 比至，超已退，朗閉門拒之。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived Chao had already withdrawn; Lang shut the gates and refused them entry.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Rutan arrived, Chao had already withdrawn, but Lang shut his gates and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 何檀怒，將攻之，鎮北將軍俱延諫曰：「安土重遷，人之常情。

translations.literal: He Tan was enraged and was about to attack; Defender of the North Juyan remonstrated: "To cherish one's native soil and dread removal is the common feeling of men.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was furious and prepared to attack. Defender of the North Juyan remonstrated, "Love of home is human nature.

sentences.zh: 朗孤城無食，今年不降，後年自服，何必多殺士卒以攻之！

translations.literal: Lang is a lone city without food; if he does not submit this year, in the year after he will submit of himself—why must you kill many soldiers to attack him!
translations.idiomatic: Lang holds a lone city without grain. If he does not yield this year, he will submit the year after. Why spend soldiers' lives to storm him!

sentences.zh: 若其不捷，彼必去從他國。

translations.literal: If you do not succeed, he will surely depart to follow another state.
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, he will flee to another power.

sentences.zh: 棄州境士民以資鄰敵，非計也；

translations.literal: To abandon the people and soil of the prefecture to supply a neighboring enemy is no plan;
translations.idiomatic: To drive away the people of our province and strengthen a rival is poor strategy;

sentences.zh: 不如以善言諭之。」

translations.literal: better to use kind words to instruct him."
translations.idiomatic: better to win him with fair words."

sentences.zh: 檀乃與朗連和，遂曜兵姑臧，壁於胡阬。

translations.literal: Rutan then made alliance with Lang, and thereupon displayed troops at Guzang and encamped at Huyan.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan then made peace with Lang, marched his army to Guzang, and encamped at Huyan.

sentences.zh: 辱檀知呂超必來斫營，畜火以待之。

translations.literal: Rutan knew Lü Chao would surely come to raid the camp and stored fire awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan knew Lü Chao would try a night raid and prepared fires to receive him.

sentences.zh: 超夜遣中{畾土}將軍王集帥精兵二千斫辱檀營，辱檀徐嚴不起。

translations.literal: At night Chao sent Central Rampart General Wang Ji leading two thousand picked troops to raid Rutan's camp; Rutan slowly tightened discipline and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chao sent Central Rampart General Wang Ji with two thousand elite troops to strike Rutan's camp. Rutan held his men in strict order and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 集入壘中，內外皆舉火，光照如晝；

translations.literal: Ji entered the rampart; inside and outside all raised fire, illumination like daytime;
translations.idiomatic: When Ji entered the stockade, fires blazed inside and out until the night shone like day;

sentences.zh: 縱兵擊之，斬集及甲首三百餘級。

translations.literal: they loosed troops to strike them and beheaded Ji and more than three hundred heads of armor.
translations.idiomatic: then Rutan's men fell upon them and killed Ji along with more than three hundred armored officers and men.

sentences.zh: 呂隆懼，偽與檀通好，請於苑內結盟，辱檀遣俱延入盟，俱延疑其有伏，毀苑牆而入。

translations.literal: Lü Long feared, feigned alliance with Rutan, and asked to ally in the park garden; Rutan sent Juyan in to ally; Juyan suspected an ambush and broke through the park wall to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long grew afraid and pretended to make peace with Rutan, proposing an alliance in the royal park. Rutan sent Juyan to the ceremony. Juyan suspected a trap and entered by breaking through the park wall.

sentences.zh: 超伏兵擊之，俱延失馬步走，水夌江將軍郭祖力戰拒之，俱延乃得免。

translations.literal: Chao had hidden troops strike them; Juyan lost his horse and fled on foot; Shui Lingjiang General Guo Zu fought desperately to hold them off, and only then did Juyan escape.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's ambush struck. Juyan lost his horse and fled on foot. General Guo Zu of the Shui Ling River fought desperately to cover him, and Juyan barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 辱檀怒，攻其昌松太守孟示韋於顯美。

translations.literal: Rutan was enraged and attacked his Changsong Administrator Meng Shiwei at Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Rutan attacked Changsong governor Meng Shiwei at Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 隆遣廣武將軍荀安國、寧遠將軍石可帥騎五百救之。

translations.literal: Long sent General Who Spreads Martial Xun Anguo and General Who Pacifies the Distance Shi Ke leading five hundred cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Long sent General Who Spreads Martial Xun Anguo and General Who Pacifies the Distance Shi Ke with five hundred horsemen to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 安國等憚辱檀之強，遁還。

translations.literal: Anguo and the others feared Rutan's strength and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo and his men feared Rutan's strength and retreated without fighting.

sentences.zh: 桓玄表其兄偉為江州刺史，鎮夏口；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan memorialized to appoint his elder brother Wei Governor of Jiang Province, stationed at Xiakou;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan memorialized to have his elder brother Wei made governor of Jiang province and stationed at Xiakou;

sentences.zh: 司馬刁暢為輔國將軍、督八郡軍事，鎮襄陽；

translations.literal: Sima Diao Chang as General Who Supports the State, Superintendent of Military Affairs for Eight Commanderies, stationed at Xiangyang;
