translations.idiomatic: He made Sima Diao Chang general who supports the state, superintendent of military affairs for eight commanderies, and stationed him at Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 遣其將皇甫敷、馮該戍湓口。

translations.literal: he sent his generals Huangfu Fu and Feng Gai to garrison Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: and sent his generals Huangfu Fu and Feng Gai to garrison Penkou.

sentences.zh: 移沮、漳蠻二千戶於江南，立武寧郡；

translations.literal: He moved two thousand households of the Ju and Zhang barbarians south of the Yangtze and established Wuning Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He moved two thousand households of the Ju and Zhang tribes south of the Yangtze and established Wuning commandery;

sentences.zh: 更招集流民，立綏安郡。

translations.literal: again he gathered displaced people and established Suian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: then gathered more displaced people and established Suian commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔征廣州刺史刁逵、豫章太守郭昶之，玄皆留不遣。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Guangzhou Inspector Diao Kui and Yuzhang Administrator Guo Changzhi, but Xuan detained them all and would not send them.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Guangzhou inspector Diao Kui and Yuzhang administrator Guo Changzhi, but Xuan held them back and refused to let them go.

sentences.zh: 玄自謂有晉國三分之二，數使人上己符瑞，欲以惑眾；

translations.literal: Xuan considered himself to possess two-thirds of the Jin realm, repeatedly sent men to present portents and auspicious signs concerning himself, wishing thereby to delude the masses;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed he held two-thirds of the Jin realm and repeatedly sent men to report omens and auspicious signs about himself, hoping to mislead the people;

sentences.zh: 又致箋於會稽王道子曰：「賊造近郊，以風不得進，以雨不致火，食盡故去耳，非力屈也。

translations.literal: also he sent a letter to Kuaiji Prince Sima Daozi, saying: "The bandits came near the suburbs; because wind would not let them advance and rain would not let them set fires, their food ran out so they left—this was not because their strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi: "The rebels reached the suburbs, but wind kept them from advancing and rain kept them from setting fires; they left only because their provisions were exhausted, not because they were beaten.

sentences.zh: 昔國寶死後，王恭不乘此威入統朝政，足見其心非侮於明公也，而謂之不忠。

translations.literal: In the past after Guobao died, Wang Gong did not use this power to enter and take charge of court affairs—this is sufficient to show his heart did not treat Your Grace with contempt, yet he was called disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: After Guobao died, Wang Gong did not use that moment to seize control of the court—enough to show he did not slight you—yet he was called disloyal.

sentences.zh: 今之貴要腹心，有時流清望者誰乎？

translations.literal: Among today's honored and powerful confidants, who has the pure reputation of present renown?
translations.idiomatic: Among the great men at court today, who still enjoys the esteem of the age?

sentences.zh: 豈可雲無佳勝！

translations.literal: How can one say there are no excellent men!
translations.idiomatic: Surely you cannot say there are no worthy men!

sentences.zh: 直是不能信之耳！

translations.literal: It is simply that they cannot be trusted!
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is simply that they cannot be trusted!

sentences.zh: 爾來一朝一夕，遂成今日之禍。

translations.literal: In recent days morning and night, today's disaster was thus formed.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day, night by night, the disaster of today has taken shape.

sentences.zh: 在朝君子皆畏禍不言，玄忝任在遠，是以披寫事實。」

translations.literal: The gentlemen at court all fear disaster and do not speak; Xuan, holding office at a distance, therefore lays bare the facts."
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen at court all fear calamity and keep silent; I, unworthy though I am, hold office far away, and therefore lay bare the truth."

sentences.zh: 元顯見之，大懼。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xian saw it, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xian read it, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 張法順謂元顯曰：「桓玄承籍世資，素有豪氣，既並殷、揚，專有荊楚，第下之所控引止三吳耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Fashun said to Yuan Xian: "Huan Xuan inherits generations of resources and has always had a bold spirit; having absorbed Yin and Yang, he alone possesses Jing and Chu—what you control amounts only to the Three Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fashun said to Yuan Xian, "Huan Xuan draws on generations of power and has always been bold. Having taken Yin and Yang, he holds Jing and Chu alone, while you command only the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫恩為亂，東土塗地，公私困竭，玄必乘此縱其奸凶，竊用憂之。」

translations.literal: Sun En's rebellion has smeared the eastern lands; public and private are exhausted—Xuan is sure to take advantage of this to unleash his treachery—I privately use worry about this."
translations.idiomatic: Sun En has ravaged the east; public and private resources are spent. Xuan is sure to seize this moment to unleash his villainy. I venture to say I am deeply worried."

sentences.zh: 元顯曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: Yuan Xian said, "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian said, "What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 法順曰：「玄始得荊州，人情未附。

translations.literal: Fashun said, "Xuan has only just obtained Jing Province; hearts are not yet attached.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun said, "Xuan has only just taken Jing province; the people are not yet loyal to him.

sentences.zh: 方務綏撫，未暇他圖。

translations.literal: He is busy with pacification and has no leisure for other designs.
translations.idiomatic: He is busy winning them over and has no time for other schemes.

sentences.zh: 若乘此際使劉牢之為前鋒，而第下以大軍繼進，玄可取也。」

translations.literal: If you seize this moment and make Liu Laozhi the vanguard while you follow with a great army, Xuan can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: If you seize this moment, make Liu Laozhi the vanguard, and follow with your main force, Xuan can be taken."

sentences.zh: 元顯以為然。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian agreed.

sentences.zh: 會武昌太守庾楷以玄與朝廷構怨，恐事不成，禍及於己，密使人自結於元顯，云：「玄大失人情，眾不為用，若朝廷遣軍，己當為內應。」

translations.literal: It happened that Wuchang Administrator Yu Kai, because Xuan and the court bore mutual resentment, feared matters would not succeed and disaster would reach him, secretly sent someone to ally himself with Yuan Xian, saying: "Xuan has greatly lost popular sentiment; the masses will not serve him—if the court sends troops, I shall act as inner collaborator."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wuchang administrator Yu Kai, fearing that Xuan's quarrel with the court would fail and ruin him, secretly sent a man to Yuan Xian offering alliance: "Xuan has lost the people's hearts; no one will fight for him. If the court sends an army, I will act as your man inside."

sentences.zh: 元顯大喜，遣張法順至京口，謀於劉牢之；

translations.literal: Yuan Xian was greatly pleased and sent Zhang Fashun to Jingkou to consult with Liu Laozhi;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian was delighted and sent Zhang Fashun to Jingkou to consult Liu Laozhi;

sentences.zh: 牢之以為難。

translations.literal: Laozhi considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi thought the plan hard to carry out.

sentences.zh: 法順還，謂元顯曰：「觀牢之言色，必貳於我，不如召入殺之；

translations.literal: Fashun returned and said to Yuan Xian: "Judging Laozhi's words and expression, he will surely turn against us—better summon him in and kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Fashun returned and told Yuan Xian, "From Laozhi's words and manner he is sure to betray us. Better summon him and kill him;

sentences.zh: 不爾，敗人大事。」

translations.literal: otherwise you will ruin the great affair."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will ruin everything."

sentences.zh: 元顯不從。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian refused.

sentences.zh: 於是大治水軍，徵兵裝艦，以謀討玄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly built a water army, levied troops and fitted out ships, to plan an expedition against Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he built up the river fleet, levied troops, and fitted out warships to attack Xuan.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝丁元興元年（壬寅，公元四零二年） 。

translations.literal: First year of Yuanxing of Emperor An (renyin, AD 402).
translations.idiomatic: First year of Yuanxing of Emperor An (renyin, AD 402).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚午朔，下詔罪狀桓玄，以尚書令元顯為驃騎大將軍、征討大都督、都督十八州諸軍事，加黃鉞，又以鎮北將軍劉牢之為前鋒都督，前將軍譙王尚之為後部，因大赦，改元，內外戒嚴；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day gengwu, an edict listed Huan Xuan's crimes; Director of the Secretariat Yuan Xian was made Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Grand Commander of the punitive campaign, Superintendent of Military Affairs for Eighteen Provinces, with the yellow battle-axe added; Northern Pacification General Liu Laozhi was made vanguard commander and Forward General Prince of Qiao Shangzhi the rear; thereupon a general amnesty, a change of reign title, and alert within and without;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengwu, the new moon, an edict condemned Huan Xuan. Yuan Xian, director of the secretariat, was made rapid-cavalry grand general, grand commander of the punitive campaign, and superintendent of military affairs for eighteen provinces, with the yellow battle-axe added. Northern pacification general Liu Laozhi was made vanguard commander and forward general Prince Shangzhi of Qiao the rear. A general amnesty followed, the reign title was changed, and the realm was placed on alert;

sentences.zh: 加會稽王道子太傅。

translations.literal: Kuaiji Prince Sima Daozi was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi was made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 元顯欲盡誅諸桓。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian wished to execute all the Huans.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian wanted to execute every member of the Huan clan.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桓修，驃騎長史王誕之甥也，誕有寵於元顯，因陳修等與玄志趣不同，元顯乃止。

translations.literal: Central Protector of the Army Huan Xiu was a nephew of Rapid Cavalry Chief Clerk Wang Dan; Dan had favor with Yuan Xian, and through stating that Xiu and the others did not share Xuan's aims Yuan Xian then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Central protector of the army Huan Xiu was a nephew of rapid-cavalry chief clerk Wang Dan. Dan enjoyed Yuan Xian's favor and argued that Xiu and the others did not share Xuan's designs, so Yuan Xian relented.

sentences.zh: 誕，導之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was a great-grandson of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a great-grandson of Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 張法順言於元顯曰：「桓謙兄弟每為上流耳目，宜斬之以杜奸謀。

translations.literal: Zhang Fashun said to Yuan Xian: "The brothers Huan Qian are always the eyes and ears of the upper reaches; they should be beheaded to block treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fashun said to Yuan Xian, "The brothers Huan Qian are the eyes and ears of the upper Yangtze. Cut off their heads to forestall treachery.

sentences.zh: 且事之濟不，繫在前軍，而牢之反覆，萬一有變，則禍敗立至。

translations.literal: Moreover whether the affair succeeds or not depends on the vanguard army, yet Laozhi is fickle—if by any chance there is a change, disaster will come at once.
translations.idiomatic: And success or failure hangs on the vanguard—yet Laozhi is unreliable. If anything goes wrong, ruin will come at once.

sentences.zh: 可令牢之殺謙兄弟以示無貳心，若不受命，當逆為其所。」

translations.literal: You can have Laozhi kill the Qian brothers to show he has no second heart; if he does not accept the order, you should act against him in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Have Laozhi kill the Qian brothers to prove his loyalty. If he refuses, move against him first."

sentences.zh: 元顯曰：「今非牢之，無以知玄；

translations.literal: Yuan Xian said, "Now without Laozhi there is no knowing Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian said, "Without Laozhi we cannot take on Xuan;

sentences.zh: 且始事而誅大將，人情不安。」

translations.literal: moreover to execute a great general at the very start would unsettle hearts."
translations.idiomatic: and to kill a great general at the outset would unsettle the army."

sentences.zh: 再三不可。

translations.literal: Again and again he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun pressed him again and again, but Yuan Xian would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又以桓氏世為荊土所附，桓沖特有遺惠，而謙，沖之子也，乃自驃騎司馬除都督荊、益、寧、梁四州諸軍事、荊州刺史，欲以結西人之心。

translations.literal: Moreover the Huan clan for generations had been attached to by the people of Jing, and Huan Chong in particular had left a legacy of kindness; Qian was Chong's son—therefore from Rapid Cavalry Marshal he was removed and made Superintendent of Military Affairs for the four provinces of Jing, Yi, Ning, and Liang and Governor of Jing Province, wishing thereby to win the hearts of the westerners.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan had long been loved in Jing, and Huan Chong in particular had left the people grateful. Qian was Chong's son, so Yuan Xian moved him from rapid-cavalry marshal to superintendent of military affairs for Jing, Yi, Ning, and Liang and governor of Jing province, hoping to win over the west.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，燕慕容拔攻魏令支戍，克之，宿沓干走，執魏遼西太守那頡。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Yan's Murong Ba attacked Wei's garrison at Lingzhi, took it; Suda Gan fled, and they seized Wei's Liaoxi Administrator Na Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Murong Ba of Yan attacked Wei's garrison at Lingzhi and took it. Suda Gan fled, and they captured Wei's Liaoxi governor Na Jie.

sentences.zh: 燕以拔為幽州刺史，鎮令支，以中堅將軍遼西陽豪為本郡太守。

translations.literal: Yan made Ba Governor of You Province, stationed at Lingzhi, and Central Stalwart General Yang Hao of Liaoxi the native prefecture's administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Yan made Ba governor of You province, stationed at Lingzhi, and central stalwart general Yang Hao of Liaoxi administrator of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以章武公淵為尚書令，博陵公虔為尚書左僕射，尚書王騰為右僕射。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Zhangwu Duke Yuan was made Director of the Secretariat, Boling Duke Qian was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Director of the Secretariat Wang Teng was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Zhangwu duke Yuan was made director of the secretariat, Boling duke Qian left vice director, and Wang Teng right vice director.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏材官將國和突攻黜弗、素古延等諸部，破之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Wei's corps officer general Guo Hetu attacked the tribes of Chufu, Suguyan, and others and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Wei corps officer general Guo Hetu attacked the tribes of Chufu, Suguyan, and others and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主珪遣北部大人賀狄干獻馬千匹求昏於秦，秦王興聞珪已立慕容後，止狄干而絕其昏；

translations.literal: Earlier Wei's ruler Gui had sent the northern great man He Digan to present a thousand horses and seek marriage with Qin; Qin's ruler Xing, hearing that Gui had already established Murong Hou, detained Digan and broke off the marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei's ruler Gui had sent the northern great man He Digan with a thousand horses to seek marriage with Qin. Qin's ruler Xing, hearing that Gui had already taken Murong Hou as consort, detained Digan and broke off the match;

sentences.zh: 沒弈干、黜弗、素古延，皆秦之屬國也，而魏攻之，由是秦、魏有隙。

translations.literal: Moyigan, Chufu, and Suguyan were all Qin's dependent states, yet Wei attacked them—thereby Qin and Wei had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Moyigan, Chufu, and Suguyan were all Qin's dependent tribes, yet Wei attacked them, and from this Qin and Wei fell out.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，珪大閱士馬，命并州諸郡積穀於平陽之乾壁，以備秦。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Gui reviewed troops and horses in great array and ordered the commanderies of Bing Province to store grain at Ganbi in Pingyang, to prepare against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Gui held a great review of troops and horses and ordered the commanderies of Bing to store grain at Ganbi in Pingyang against Qin.

sentences.zh: 柔然社侖方睦於秦，遣將救黜弗、素古延；

translations.literal: Rouran Shelun was just then on friendly terms with Qin and sent generals to rescue Chufu and Suguyan;
translations.idiomatic: Rouran Shelun was then on good terms with Qin and sent generals to rescue Chufu and Suguyan;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，和突逆擊，大破之，社帥侖其部落遠遁漠北，奪高車之地而居之。

translations.literal: on xinmao, Hetu counterattacked and routed them greatly; Shelun led his tribes in flight far into the northern desert and seized the Gaoche lands to dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: on xinmao, Hetu counterattacked and routed them. Shelun led his tribes in flight far into the northern desert, seized Gaoche territory, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 斛律部帥倍侯利擊社侖，大為所敗，倍侯利奔魏。

translations.literal: The chief of the Hulu tribe, Beihouli, attacked Shelun and was greatly defeated by him; Beihouli fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli, chief of the Hulu tribe, attacked Shelun and was badly beaten; Beihouli fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 社侖於是西北擊匈奴遺種日拔也雞，大破之，遂吞併諸部，士馬繁盛，雄於北方。

translations.literal: Shelun thereupon struck northwest at the Xiongnu remnant Ribayeji, routed him greatly, then swallowed up the various tribes; soldiers and horses flourished, and he was mighty in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun then struck northwest at the Xiongnu remnant Ribayeji and crushed him, swallowed the other tribes, and his warriors and horses flourished until he dominated the north.

sentences.zh: 其地西至焉耆，東接朝鮮，南臨大漠，旁側小國皆羈屬焉。

translations.literal: His lands reached west to Yanqi, east joined Korea, south faced the great desert, and the small states on every side were all bound to him.
translations.idiomatic: His domain ran west to Yanqi, east to Korea, south to the great desert, and the lesser states on every side submitted.

sentences.zh: 自號豆代可汗。

translations.literal: He styled himself Khaghan Doudai.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Khaghan Doudai.

sentences.zh: 始立約束，以千人為軍，軍有將；

translations.literal: He first established regulations: a thousand men formed an army, and an army had a commander;
translations.idiomatic: He first set down laws: a thousand men made an army, and each army had a commander;

sentences.zh: 百人為幢，幢有帥。

translations.literal: a hundred men formed a banner, and a banner had a chief.
translations.idiomatic: a hundred men made a banner, and each banner had a chief.

sentences.zh: 攻戰先登者賜以虜獲，畏懦者以石擊其首而殺之。

translations.literal: In battle those who charged first were rewarded with captives; the cowardly had their heads struck with stones and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In battle those who charged first received the spoils; cowards were killed by having stones hurled at their heads.

sentences.zh: 禿髮示韋檀克顯美，執孟示韋而責之，以其不早降。

translations.literal: Tufa Rutan took Xianmei, seized Meng Shiwei and reproached him for not having surrendered earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan took Xianmei, seized Meng Shiwei, and rebuked him for not surrendering sooner.

sentences.zh: 示韋曰：「示韋受呂氏厚恩，分符守土；

translations.literal: Shiwei said: "Shiwei received the Lü clan's deep favor and held a tally to guard the land;
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei said, "I received deep favor from the Lü clan and held a commission to guard this land;

sentences.zh: 若明公大軍甫至，望旗歸附，恐獲罪於執事矣。」

translations.literal: if when Your Grace's great army had just arrived I had lowered my banner and submitted, I feared I would incur guilt before those in charge."
translations.idiomatic: if when your great army had barely arrived I had lowered my banner and submitted, I feared I would be judged guilty by my superiors."

sentences.zh: 示韋檀釋而禮之，徙二千餘戶而歸，以示韋為左司馬。

translations.literal: Rutan released and honored him, moved more than two thousand households back, and made Shiwei Left Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan released him with honor, moved more than two thousand households back with him, and made Shiwei left marshal.

sentences.zh: 示韋辭曰：「呂氏將亡，聖朝必取河右，人無愚智皆知之。

translations.literal: Shiwei declined, saying: "The Lü clan is about to perish; the sage court is sure to take the lands west of the Yellow River—there is none foolish or wise who does not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwei declined: "The Lü are about to fall; the sage court is sure to take the lands west of the River. Everyone knows it.

sentences.zh: 但示韋為人守城不能全，復忝顯任，於心竊所未安。

translations.literal: Yet Shiwei, in guarding a city for others, could not preserve it whole, and again bears a conspicuous post—in my heart I have never been at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I held a city for another and could not keep it intact, and now you would honor me again—I cannot accept it in good conscience.

sentences.zh: 若蒙明公之惠，使得就戮姑臧，死且不朽。」

translations.literal: If I receive Your Grace's kindness and am allowed to go to Guzang for execution, death would not perish."
translations.idiomatic: If you grant me your kindness and let me go to Guzang to die, my death will not be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 示韋檀義而歸之。

translations.literal: Rutan, moved by righteousness, sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his integrity, Rutan sent him back.

sentences.zh: 東土遭孫恩之亂，因以饑饉，漕運不繼。

translations.literal: The eastern lands had suffered Sun En's disorder and thereby famine; grain transport by water did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: The east had been ravaged by Sun En's rebellion and then by famine; grain transport by water ceased.

sentences.zh: 桓玄禁斷江路，商旅俱絕，公私匱乏，以稃、橡給士卒。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan blocked the Yangtze routes; merchants and travelers all ceased; public and private were depleted, and husked grain and acorns were given to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan cut the Yangtze routes; trade stopped; public and private stores ran dry, and the troops were fed on chaff and acorns.

sentences.zh: 玄謂朝廷方多憂虞，必未暇討己，可以蓄力觀釁。

translations.literal: Xuan thought the court had many worries and would surely have no leisure to attack him, and could store strength and watch for openings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan thought the court had too many troubles to attack him and could gather strength while waiting for his chance.

sentences.zh: 及大軍將發，從兄太傅長史石生密以書報之。

translations.literal: When the great army was about to set out, his cousin the Grand Tutor's Chief Clerk Shi Sheng secretly sent a letter reporting it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army was about to march, his cousin the grand tutor's chief clerk Shi Sheng secretly wrote to warn him.

sentences.zh: 玄大驚，欲完聚保江陵。

translations.literal: Xuan was greatly alarmed and wished to gather his forces and hold Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was alarmed and wanted to mass his forces and hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 長史卞范之曰：「明公英威振於遠近，元顯口尚乳臭，劉牢之大失物情，若兵臨近畿，示以禍福，土崩之勢可翹足而待，何有延敵入境，自取窮蹙者乎！」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Bian Fanzhi said: "Your Grace's heroic might shakes far and near; Yuan Xian's mouth still smells of milk; Liu Laozhi has greatly lost popular sentiment—if troops press the near capital and show fortune and disaster, a landslide can be awaited with a lifted foot—why prolong the enemy's entry and bring distress on yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Bian Fanzhi said, "Your heroic name shakes the realm. Yuan Xian still smells of milk. Liu Laozhi has lost the people's hearts. March on the capital, show them blessing or ruin, and they will collapse before you lift a foot. Why let the enemy in and corner yourself?"

sentences.zh: 玄從之，留桓偉守江陵，抗表傳檄，罪狀元顯，舉兵東下。

translations.literal: Xuan followed this, left Huan Wei to guard Jiangling, submitted a memorial and circulated a proclamation listing Yuan Xian's crimes, and raised troops marching east.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan agreed, left Huan Wei to guard Jiangling, memorialized and issued a proclamation condemning Yuan Xian, and marched east with his army.

sentences.zh: 檄至，元顯大懼。

translations.literal: When the proclamation arrived, Yuan Xian was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation arrived, Yuan Xian was terrified.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙午，帝餞元顯於西池，元顯下船而不發。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingwu, the Emperor saw Yuan Xian off at the West Pond; Yuan Xian boarded the ship but did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingwu, the emperor saw Yuan Xian off at the West Pond. Yuan Xian boarded his ship but would not sail.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏常山王遵等至高平，沒弈干棄其部眾，帥數千騎與劉勃勃奔秦州。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wei's Prince of Changshan Zun and others reached Gaoping; Moyigan abandoned his tribes, leading several thousand horsemen with Liu Bobo to flee to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Wei's prince of Changshan Zun and others reached Gaoping. Moyigan abandoned his tribes and fled to Qinzhou with several thousand horsemen and Liu Bobo.

sentences.zh: 魏軍追至瓦亭，不及而還，盡獲其府庫蓄積，馬四萬餘匹，雜畜九萬餘口，徙其民於代都，餘種分迸。

translations.literal: The Wei army pursued to Wating, could not overtake them and returned, fully obtaining their treasury stores, more than forty thousand horses, and more than ninety thousand head of mixed livestock; they moved the people to the capital of Dai, and the remaining clans scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army pursued to Wating, failed to catch them, and returned with all their stores, more than forty thousand horses, and more than ninety thousand head of livestock. The people were moved to the capital of Dai and the remnant tribes scattered.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守貳塵復侵秦河東，長安大震，關中諸城晝閉，秦人簡兵訓卒以謀伐魏。

translations.literal: Pingyang Administrator Er Chen again invaded Qin's Hedong; Chang'an was greatly shaken, the passes' cities closed by day, and the people of Qin selected troops and trained soldiers to plan an attack on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang administrator Er Chen again invaded Qin's Hedong. Chang'an was shaken; the passes' cities closed by day; and Qin mustered and trained troops to attack Wei.

sentences.zh: 秦王興立子泓為太子，大赦。

translations.literal: Qin's ruler Xing established his son Hong as heir and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's ruler Xing made his son Hong heir apparent and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 泓孝友寬和，喜文學，善談詠，而懦弱多病。

translations.literal: Hong was filial, friendly, broad and mild, fond of literature, skilled in discourse and recitation, yet timid and often ill.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was filial, friendly, broad-minded, and mild, fond of letters and skilled at talk and song, yet timid and often ill.

sentences.zh: 興欲以為嗣，而狐疑不決，久乃立之。

translations.literal: Xing wished to make him heir yet hesitated and could not decide; only after long delay did he establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Xing wanted him as heir but hesitated for a long time before at last naming him.

sentences.zh: 姑臧大饑，米斗直錢五千，人相食，饑死者十餘萬口。

translations.literal: At Guzang there was great famine; rice cost five thousand cash per dou, and people ate one another; those who starved numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guzang suffered great famine. A dou of rice cost five thousand cash. People ate one another, and more than a hundred thousand starved.

sentences.zh: 城門晝閉，樵采路絕，民請出城為胡虜奴婢者，日有數百，呂隆惡其沮動眾心，盡坑之，積屍盈路。

translations.literal: The city gates were closed by day, firewood-gathering routes were cut off, and people who begged to leave the city to become slaves of the barbarians numbered hundreds each day; Lü Long hated that this would shake the people's hearts and buried them all alive; corpses piled along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were shut by day and firewood routes cut off. Hundreds each day begged to leave and become barbarian slaves. Lü Long, fearing this would shake morale, buried them alive until corpses filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜引兵攻姑臧，隆遣使求救於河西王利鹿孤，利鹿孤遣廣武公辱檀帥騎一萬救之，未至，隆擊破蒙遜軍，蒙遜請與隆盟，留谷萬餘斛遣之而還。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun led troops to attack Guzang; Long sent envoys to seek rescue from Hexi King Lilugu, who sent Duke of Guangwu Rutan with ten thousand horsemen to save him; before they arrived, Long defeated Mengxun's army; Mengxun asked to ally with Long, left more than ten thousand hu of grain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun attacked Guzang. Long sent for help to Hexi king Lilugu, who sent Duke of Guangwu Rutan with ten thousand horsemen. Before they arrived, Long beat Mengxun's army. Mengxun sued for peace, left more than ten thousand hu of grain, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辱檀至昌松，聞蒙遜已退，乃徙澤段塚民五百餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Rutan reached Changsong; hearing Mengxun had withdrawn, he moved more than five hundred households of the Ze segment tombs and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan reached Changsong. Hearing Mengxun had withdrawn, he moved more than five hundred households from the Ze segment tombs and returned.

sentences.zh: 中散騎常侍張融言於利鹿孤曰：「焦朗兄弟據魏安，潛通姚氏，數為反覆，今不取，後必為朝廷憂。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant in Regular Service Zhang Rong spoke to Lilugu, saying: "The Jiao Lang brothers hold Weian, secretly communicate with the Yao clan, and have repeatedly been inconstant; if we do not take them now, later they will surely be a worry for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhang Rong said to Lilugu, "The Jiao Lang brothers hold Weian, secretly deal with the Yao, and have turned coat again and again. If we do not seize them now, they will surely trouble the court later.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤遣辱檀討之，朗面縛出降，辱檀送於西平，徙其民於樂都。

translations.literal: Lilugu sent Rutan to attack them; Lang came out bound with his face in bonds to surrender; Rutan sent him to Xiping and moved the people to Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu sent Rutan against them. Lang came out with bonds on his face and surrendered. Rutan sent him to Xiping and moved the people to Ledu.

sentences.zh: 桓玄發江陵，慮事不捷，常為西還之計。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan set out from Jiangling; fearing matters would not succeed, he often made plans for a westward retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan marched from Jiangling. Fearing defeat, he kept planning a retreat west.

sentences.zh: 及過尋陽，不見官軍，意甚喜，將士之氣亦振。

translations.literal: When he passed Xunyang and saw no government troops, he was greatly pleased, and the officers' and soldiers' spirits were also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang he saw no imperial army and was greatly pleased; his officers and men took heart as well.

sentences.zh: 庾楷謀洩，玄囚之。

translations.literal: Yu Kai's plot was leaked; Xuan imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai's plot leaked out, and Xuan had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔遣齊王柔之以騶虞幡宣告荊、江二州，使罷兵；

translations.literal: On dingsi, an edict sent Prince of Qi Rouzhi with the Zo Yu banner to proclaim to Jing and Jiang provinces, ordering the armies to stand down;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, an edict dispatched Prince of Qi Rouzhi with the Zo Yu peace banner to proclaim to Jing and Jiang that the armies must stand down;

sentences.zh: 玄前鋒殺之。

translations.literal: Xuan's vanguard killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's vanguard killed him.

sentences.zh: 柔之，宗之子也。

translations.literal: Rouzhi was a son of Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Rouzhi was a son of Zong.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，玄至姑孰，使共將馮該等攻歷陽，襄城太守司馬休之嬰城固守。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Xuan reached Gudu and sent joint general Feng Gai and others to attack Liyang; Xiangcheng prefect Sima Xiuzhi shut the city gates and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Xuan reached Gudu and sent Feng Gai and other joint generals against Liyang. Xiangcheng prefect Sima Xiuzhi barred the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 玄軍斷洞浦，焚豫州舟艦。

translations.literal: Xuan's army cut off Dongpu and burned Yuzhou's boats.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's army severed Dongpu and burned the boats of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史譙王尚之帥步卒九千陣於浦上，遣武都太守楊秋屯橫江，秋降於玄軍。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Prince of Qiao Shangzhi led nine thousand infantry in formation on the shore, sent Wudu prefect Yang Qiu to garrison Hengjiang; Qiu surrendered to Xuan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Prince of Qiao Shangzhi drew up nine thousand foot soldiers on the shore and sent Wudu prefect Yang Qiu to hold Hengjiang. Qiu surrendered to Xuan's army.

sentences.zh: 尚之眾潰，逃於塗中，玄捕獲之。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's forces collapsed and fled along the roads; Xuan captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's troops broke and fled along the roads. Xuan captured him.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之出戰而敗，棄城走。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi went out to battle and was defeated, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi gave battle and was beaten; he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之素惡驃騎大將軍元顯，恐桓玄既滅，元顯益驕恣，又恐己功名愈盛，不為元顯所容，且自恃材武，擁強兵，欲假玄以除執政，復伺玄之隙而自取之，故不肯討玄。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi had long hated General of Agile Cavalry Yuan Xian; he feared that once Huan Xuan was destroyed Yuan Xian would grow even more arrogant and unrestrained, and also feared that as his own merit grew greater he would not be tolerated by Yuan Xian; moreover trusting in his own talent and martial prowess and commanding strong troops, he wished to borrow Xuan to remove the ruling power, then watch for an opening in Xuan to take it for himself—therefore he would not attack Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi had long hated General of Agile Cavalry Yuan Xian. He feared that if Huan Xuan fell, Yuan Xian would grow still more arrogant, and that his own rising fame would make Yuan Xian unable to bear him. Trusting his martial gifts and strong army, he meant to use Xuan to remove the rulers, then watch for a gap and seize power himself. For that reason he would not fight Xuan.

sentences.zh: 元顯日夜昏酣，以牢之為前鋒。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian day and night drank in drunken stupor, making Laozhi vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian spent his days and nights in drunken stupor and made Laozhi his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 牢之驟詣門，不得見，及帝出餞元顯，遇之公坐而已。

translations.literal: Laozhi repeatedly came to the gate but was not granted audience; only when the emperor came out to send off Yuan Xian did he meet him on the open dais—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi came again and again to the gate but was refused audience. Only when the emperor came out to send Yuan Xian off did he meet him on the open dais—and no more.

sentences.zh: 牢之軍溧洲，參軍劉裕請擊玄，牢之不許。

translations.literal: Laozhi's army was at Lizhou; staff officer Liu Yu asked to attack Xuan; Laozhi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi's army was at Lizhou. Staff officer Liu Yu asked to strike Xuan, but Laozhi would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 玄使牢之族舅何穆說牢之曰：「自古戴震主之威，挾不賞之功而能自全者，誰邪？

translations.literal: Xuan sent Laozhi's clan uncle He Mu to persuade Laozhi, saying: "Since antiquity, who has worn the awe of shock-ruling the lord, held merit beyond reward, and yet been able to preserve himself whole?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Laozhi's clan uncle He Mu to persuade him, saying, "Since antiquity, who has worn the terror of overawing his lord, held merit too great to reward, and still kept himself whole?

sentences.zh: 越之文種，秦之白起，漢之韓信，皆事明主，為之盡力，功成之日，猶不免誅夷，況為凶愚者之用乎！

translations.literal: Wen Zhong of Yue, Bai Qi of Qin, and Han Xin of Han—all served enlightened rulers and did their utmost for them; on the day their achievements were complete they still could not avoid execution and extermination of kin—how much less when employed by a vicious fool!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhong of Yue, Bai Qi of Qin, Han Xin of Han—all served enlightened rulers and gave their all, yet on the day their work was done they still could not escape execution and the ruin of their clans. How much less when serving a vicious fool!

sentences.zh: 君如今日戰勝則傾宗，戰敗則覆族，欲以此安歸乎！

translations.literal: Sir, if you win today you will overturn your clan; if you lose you will destroy your family—where do you intend to return in safety!
translations.idiomatic: If you win today you overturn your clan; if you lose you destroy your family. Where can you go in safety?

sentences.zh: 不若翻然改圖，則可以長保富貴矣。

translations.literal: Better to turn your plans about at once, and then you may long preserve wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Better turn your plans at once, and you may long keep wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 古人射鉤、斬祛，猶不害為輔佐，況玄與君無宿昔之怨乎！」

translations.literal: The ancients who shot the hook and cut the sleeve were still not barred from becoming ministers—how much less does Xuan bear an old grudge against you!
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who shot the hook or cut the sleeve still became ministers without harm. How much less does Xuan bear an old grudge against you!

sentences.zh: 時譙王尚之已敗，人情愈恐，牢之頗納穆言，與玄交通。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qiao Shangzhi had already been defeated, popular sentiment grew more fearful, and Laozhi largely accepted Mu's words and communicated with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Prince of Qiao Shangzhi had already been defeated and fear spread through the ranks. Laozhi largely took Mu's counsel and opened communications with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 東海中尉東海何無忌，牢之之甥也，與劉裕極諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Overseer of the Eastern Sea He Wuji of Donghai—Laozhi's nephew—and Liu Yu remonstrated strenuously; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji of Donghai, overseer of the Eastern Sea and Laozhi's nephew, remonstrated with Liu Yu to the utmost, but Laozhi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其子驃騎從事中郎敬宣諫曰：「今國家衰危，天下之重在大人與玄。

translations.literal: His son Attendant at the Secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry Jingxuan remonstrated, saying: "Now the state is in decline and peril; the weight of the realm lies between you, father, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxuan, attendant at the secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry, remonstrated, saying, "The state is failing and in peril. The fate of the realm rests between you, father, and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄藉父、叔之資，據有全楚，割晉國三分之二，一朝縱之使陵朝廷，玄威望既成，恐難圖也，董卓之變，將在今矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan relies on the resources of his father and uncles, holds all of Chu, has carved off two-thirds of the Jin realm; if in a morning you let him rampage against the court, once Xuan's prestige is established I fear he will be hard to plot against—the Dong Zhuo transformation will come today.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan draws on the standing of his father and uncles, holds all Chu, and has carved away two-thirds of Jin. If in a single morning you let him ride over the court, once his prestige is set I fear he will be hard to plot against. The Dong Zhuo disaster will come today.

sentences.zh: 牢之怒曰：「吾豈不知！

translations.literal: Laozhi angrily said: "Do I not know this!
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi said angrily, "Do I not know that!

sentences.zh: 今日取玄如反覆手耳；

translations.literal: Today to take Xuan is like turning the hand back and forth;
translations.idiomatic: Today to take Xuan is like turning the hand over;

sentences.zh: 但平玄之後，令我奈驃騎何！」

translations.literal: but after pacifying Xuan, what am I to do about the General of Agile Cavalry!
translations.idiomatic: but after Xuan is pacified, what am I to do about the General of Agile Cavalry!

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳朔，牢之遣敬宣詣玄請降。

translations.literal: Third month, on yisi the first of the month, Laozhi sent Jingxuan to Xuan to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day yisi, Laozhi sent Jingxuan to Xuan to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 玄陰欲誅牢之，乃與敬宣宴飲，陳名書畫共觀之，以安悅其意；

translations.literal: Xuan secretly wished to kill Laozhi; he therefore banqueted with Jingxuan and displayed famous writings and paintings for joint viewing to settle and please his mind;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan secretly meant to kill Laozhi. He therefore feasted with Jingxuan and spread out famous writings and paintings for them to admire together, to soothe and please him;

sentences.zh: 敬宣不之覺，玄佐吏莫不相視而筆。

translations.literal: Jingxuan did not notice; Xuan's assisting clerks all looked at one another and smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan noticed nothing, while Xuan's staff exchanged glances and smiled.

sentences.zh: 玄板敬宣為咨議參軍。

translations.literal: Xuan appointed Jingxuan Consultant Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan appointed Jingxuan consultant staff officer.

sentences.zh: 元顯將發，聞玄已至新亭，棄船，退屯國子學。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian was about to set out; hearing Xuan had already reached Xinting, he abandoned the boats and withdrew to garrison the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian was about to march when he heard Xuan had reached Xinting. He abandoned his boats and fell back to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 辛未，陳於宣陽門外。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he arrayed outside Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he drew up his array outside Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 軍中相驚，言玄已至南桁，元顯引兵欲還宮。

translations.literal: The army was mutually alarmed, saying Xuan had already reached Nanheng; Yuan Xian led troops intending to return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Panic ran through the army with word that Xuan had reached Nanheng. Yuan Xian led his troops back toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 玄遣人拔刀隨後大呼曰：「放仗！」

translations.literal: Xuan sent men who drew swords and followed behind shouting loudly: "Drop your weapons!
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent men with drawn swords who followed close behind shouting, "Lay down your arms!

sentences.zh: 軍人皆崩潰，元顯乘馬走入東府，唯張法順一騎隨之。

translations.literal: The soldiers all collapsed and fled; Yuan Xian mounted a horse and rushed into the Eastern Residence; only Zhang Fashun on a single horse followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers broke and fled. Yuan Xian mounted a horse and dashed into the Eastern Residence, with only Zhang Fashun following on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 元顯問計於道子，道子但對之涕泣。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian asked Daozi for counsel; Daozi only wept tears in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian asked Daozi for counsel. Daozi could only answer with tears.

sentences.zh: 玄遣太傅從事中郎毛泰收元顯送新亭，縛於舫前而數之。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Grand Tutor attendant Mao Tai to seize Yuan Xian and send him to Xinting, bound him at the prow of the boat and enumerated his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Grand Tutor attendant Mao Tai to seize Yuan Xian and take him to Xinting, bound him at the prow of the boat, and recited his crimes.

sentences.zh: 元顯曰：「為王誕、張法順所誤耳。」

translations.literal: Yuan Xian said: "I was misled by Wang Dan and Zhang Fashun—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian said, "I was misled by Wang Dan and Zhang Fashun, that is all.

sentences.zh: 壬申，復隆安年號，帝遣侍中勞玄於安樂渚。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Long'an era name was restored; the emperor sent a palace attendant to console Xuan at Anle Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Long'an era name was restored. The emperor sent a palace attendant to congratulate Xuan at Anle Ford.

sentences.zh: 玄入京師，稱詔解嚴，以玄總百揆、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、錄尚書事、揚州牧、領徐、荊、江三州刺史，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: Xuan entered the capital, declared by edict that the emergency was lifted, and was made overseer of all offices, commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad, chancellor, recorder of the Secretariat, governor of Yangzhou, and concurrently inspector of Xu, Jing, and Jiang provinces, with the yellow battle-axe on loan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan entered the capital, declared by edict that the emergency was over, and was made overseer of all offices, commander-in-chief at home and abroad, chancellor, recorder of the Secretariat, governor of Yangzhou, and concurrently inspector of Xu, Jing, and Jiang, with the yellow battle-axe on loan.

sentences.zh: 玄以桓偉為荊州刺史，桓謙為尚書左僕射，桓修為徐、兗二州刺史，桓石生為江州刺史，卞范之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Xuan made Huan Wei governor of Jing, Huan Qian Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Huan Xiu inspector of Xu and Yan, Huan Shisheng inspector of Jiang, and Bian Fanzhi governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan made Huan Wei governor of Jing, Huan Qian left vice director of the Secretariat, Huan Xiu inspector of Xu and Yan, Huan Shisheng inspector of Jiang, and Bian Fanzhi governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初，玄之舉兵，侍中王謐奉詔詣玄，玄親禮之。

translations.literal: When Xuan first raised troops, palace attendant Wang Mi received the edict and went to Xuan; Xuan personally honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan first raised troops, palace attendant Wang Mi came to him on imperial orders, and Xuan received him with personal honor.

sentences.zh: 及玄輔政，以謐為中書令。

translations.literal: When Xuan assisted in government, he made Mi Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan took power he made Mi director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謐，導之孫也。

translations.literal: Mi was a grandson of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was a grandson of Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 新安太守殷仲文，覬之弟也，玄姊為仲文妻。

translations.literal: Xin'an prefect Yin Zhongwen was the younger brother of Qi; Xuan's elder sister was Zhongwen's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an prefect Yin Zhongwen was the younger brother of Yin Qi. Xuan's elder sister was Zhongwen's wife.

sentences.zh: 仲文聞玄克京師，棄郡投玄，玄以為咨議參軍。

translations.literal: Zhongwen heard Xuan had taken the capital, abandoned his commandery and joined Xuan; Xuan made him Consultant Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwen heard Xuan had taken the capital, he abandoned his commandery and joined him. Xuan made him consultant staff officer.

sentences.zh: 劉邁往見玄，玄曰：「汝不畏死，而敢來邪？」

translations.literal: Liu Mai went to see Xuan; Xuan said: "You do not fear death and yet dare to come?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mai went to see Xuan. Xuan said, "You do not fear death, yet you dare to come?

sentences.zh: 邁曰：「射鉤斬祛，並邁為三。」

translations.literal: Mai said: "Shooting the hook and cutting the sleeve—Mai makes the third.
translations.idiomatic: Mai said, "Shooting the hook and cutting the sleeve—Mai makes the third.

sentences.zh: 玄悅，以為參軍。

translations.literal: Xuan was pleased and made him staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was pleased and made him a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，有司奏會稽王道子酣縱不孝，當棄市，詔徙安成郡；

translations.literal: On guiyou, the relevant offices memorialized that Prince of Kuaiji Daozi was drunken, dissolute, and unfilial and should be executed in the market; an edict exiled him to Ancheng commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the relevant offices memorialized that Prince of Kuaiji Daozi was drunken, dissolute, and unfilial and should be executed in the market. An edict exiled him to Ancheng commandery instead;

sentences.zh: 斬元顯及東海王彥璋、譙王尚之、庾楷、張法順、毛泰等於建康市。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian and Prince of the Eastern Sea Yanzhang, Prince of Qiao Shangzhi, Yu Kai, Zhang Fashun, Mao Tai, and others were beheaded at the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian, Prince of the Eastern Sea Yanzhang, Prince of Qiao Shangzhi, Yu Kai, Zhang Fashun, Mao Tai, and others were beheaded in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 桓修為王誕固請，得流嶺南。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu pleaded earnestly for Wang Dan, who was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu pleaded earnestly for Wang Dan, who was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 玄以劉牢之為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Xuan made Liu Laozhi interior administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan made Liu Laozhi interior administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 牢之曰：「始爾，便奪我兵，禍其至矣！」

translations.literal: Laozhi said: "Just now, and already my troops are taken—disaster is surely coming!
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi said, "So soon—and already my troops are taken. Disaster is surely at hand!

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣請歸諭牢之，使受命，玄遣之。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan asked to return and persuade Laozhi to accept the order; Xuan sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan asked to return and persuade Laozhi to accept the appointment. Xuan sent him.

sentences.zh: 敬宣勸牢之襲玄，牢之猶豫不決，移屯班瀆，私告劉裕曰：「今當北就高雅之於廣陵，舉兵以匡社稷，卿能從我去乎？」

translations.literal: Jingxuan urged Laozhi to raid Xuan; Laozhi hesitated and could not decide, moved camp to Bandu, and privately told Liu Yu: "Now I shall go north to join Gao Yazhi at Guangling and raise troops to restore the altars of state—can you follow me there?
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan urged Laozhi to strike Xuan. Laozhi hesitated, moved camp to Bandu, and privately told Liu Yu, "I shall now go north to Gao Yazhi at Guangling and raise troops to restore the realm. Will you come with me?

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「將軍以勁卒數萬，望風降服，彼新得志，威震天下，朝野人情皆已去矣，廣陵豈可得至邪！

translations.literal: Yu said: "General, with tens of thousands of crack troops, surrendered at the mere sight of their approach; they have newly won their ambition and awe shakes the realm; court and countryside sentiment has all left you—how can Guangling be reached!
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "General, with tens of thousands of crack troops you surrendered at their approach. They have newly won power and their awe shakes the realm. Court and countryside have already left you. How can you reach Guangling!

sentences.zh: 裕當反服還京口耳。」

translations.literal: Yu will instead change into mourning garb and return to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: I shall put on mourning garb and return to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 何無忌謂裕曰：「我將何之？」

translations.literal: He Wuji said to Yu: "Where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji said to Yu, "Where shall I go?

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「吾觀鎮北必不免，卿可隨我還京口。

translations.literal: Yu said: "I observe that the Northern Pacifier will surely not escape harm; you may follow me back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "I see that the Northern Pacifier will not escape ruin. You may come back to Jingkou with me.

sentences.zh: 桓玄若守臣節，當與卿事之；

translations.literal: If Huan Xuan keeps to the minister's role, I shall serve him with you;
translations.idiomatic: If Huan Xuan keeps to his minister's duty, I shall serve him with you;

sentences.zh: 不然，當與卿圖之。」

translations.literal: if not, I shall plot against him with you.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I shall plot against him with you.

sentences.zh: 於是牢之大集僚佐，議據江北以討玄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Laozhi greatly gathered his staff and officers and discussed holding the north bank of the river to attack Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Laozhi gathered his staff in full council and debated holding the north bank of the Yangzi to attack Xuan.

sentences.zh: 參軍劉襲曰：「事之不可者莫大於反。

translations.literal: Staff officer Liu Xi said: "Of things that must not be done, none is greater than rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Liu Xi said, "Of things that must not be done, none is greater than rebellion.

sentences.zh: 將軍往年反王兗州，近日反司馬郎君，今復反桓公；

translations.literal: General, in former years you rebelled against the Prince of Yan and Yanzhou, recently rebelled against the Sima gentleman, and now again rebel against Duke Huan;
translations.idiomatic: General, in former years you rebelled against Wang of Yanzhou, recently against Master Sima, and now again against Duke Huan;

sentences.zh: 一人三反，何以自立！」

translations.literal: one man thrice rebel—how can he stand!
translations.idiomatic: One man rebelling thrice—how can he stand!

sentences.zh: 語畢，趨出，佐吏多散走。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he hurried out, and most assisting clerks scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished he hurried out, and most of the staff scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 牢之懼，使敬宣之京口迎家；

translations.literal: Laozhi was afraid and sent Jingxuan to Jingkou to fetch the family;
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi grew afraid and sent Jingxuan to Jingkou to bring up the family;

sentences.zh: 失期不至，牢之以為事已洩，為玄所殺，乃帥部曲北走，至新洲，縊而死。

translations.literal: missing the deadline and not arriving, Laozhi thought the matter had leaked and that Xuan would kill him; he therefore led his personal troops north, reached Xinzhou, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline passed and they did not come, Laozhi thought the plot had leaked and that Xuan would kill him. He led his personal troops north, reached Xinzhou, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 敬宣至，不暇哭，即渡江奔廣陵。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan arrived he had no time to mourn and immediately crossed the river and fled to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan arrived he had no time to mourn and at once crossed the river and fled to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 將吏共殯斂牢之，以其喪歸丹徒。

translations.literal: Generals and officials together enshrouded and buried Laozhi and brought his coffin back to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: His generals and officials together laid out Laozhi's body and brought his coffin back to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 玄令斫棺斬首，暴屍於市。

translations.literal: Xuan ordered the coffin split open and the head cut off, and the corpse exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan ordered the coffin opened, the head cut off, and the corpse exposed in the market.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元大亨。

translations.literal: General amnesty; the era name was changed to Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Daxing.

sentences.zh: 桓玄讓丞相荊、江、徐三州，改授太尉、都督中外諸軍事、揚州牧、領豫州刺史，總百揆；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan yielded the posts of chancellor and inspector of Jing, Jiang, and Xu, and was reassigned as Grand Marshal, commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad, governor of Yangzhou, and concurrently inspector of Yuzhou, overseeing all offices;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan yielded the chancellorship and the inspectorates of Jing, Jiang, and Xu, and was reassigned Grand Marshal, commander-in-chief at home and abroad, governor of Yangzhou, and concurrently inspector of Yuzhou, overseeing all offices;

sentences.zh: 以琅邪王德文為太宰。

translations.literal: Langya prince Dewen was made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langya Dewen was made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之、劉敬宣、高雅之俱奔洛陽，各以子弟為質於秦以求救。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Liu Jingxuan, and Gao Yazhi all fled to Luoyang, each sending younger kin as hostages to Qin to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Liu Jingxuan, and Gao Yazhi all fled to Luoyang and each sent younger kin as hostages to Qin to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 秦王興與之符信，使於關東募兵，得數千人，復還屯彭城間。

translations.literal: Qin's ruler Xing gave them tally-credentials and sent them to raise troops east of the passes; they got several thousand men and again encamped around Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's ruler Xing gave them credentials and sent them to raise troops east of the passes. They gathered several thousand men and encamped again around Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 孫恩寇臨海，臨海太守辛景擊破之，恩所虜三吳男女，死亡殆盡。

translations.literal: Sun En raided Linhai; Linhai prefect Xin Jing defeated him; the men and women of the three Wu regions whom En had captured died almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En raided Linhai. Linhai prefect Xin Jing defeated him. Of the men and women of the three Wu regions whom En had taken captive, nearly all perished.

sentences.zh: 恩恐為官軍所獲，乃赴海死，其黨及妓妾從死者以百數，謂之「水仙」。

translations.literal: En, fearing capture by government troops, threw himself into the sea and died; his partisans and concubines who followed him in death numbered in the hundreds—they were called "water immortals."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture by imperial troops, En threw himself into the sea and died. His followers and concubines who died with him numbered in the hundreds; they were called "water immortals."

sentences.zh: 餘眾數千人復推恩妹夫盧循為主。

translations.literal: The remaining host of several thousand again made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand survivors again made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader.

sentences.zh: 循，諶之曾孫也，神采清秀，雅有材藝。

translations.literal: Xun was a great-grandson of Chen; his bearing was refined and clear, and he had elegant talent and skill.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was a great-grandson of Lu Chen. His bearing was refined and clear, and he had elegant gifts and skill.

sentences.zh: 少時，沙門惠遠嘗謂之曰：「君雖體涉風素，而志存不軌，如何？」

translations.literal: In his youth the monk Huiyuan once said to him: "Though your person partakes of pure wind, your will harbors unrighteous designs—how so?
translations.idiomatic: In his youth the monk Huiyuan once said to him, "Though your person partakes of pure simplicity, your will harbors unrighteous designs. How can that be?

sentences.zh: 太尉玄欲撫安東土，乃以循為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Xuan wished to pacify the eastern lands and therefore made Xun prefect of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Xuan wished to pacify the eastern lands and therefore made Xun prefect of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 循雖受命，而寇暴不已。

translations.literal: Although Xun had received his appointment, bandit raids and violence did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lu Xun had accepted the appointment, plunder and violence went on unchecked.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，燕大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Yan granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 河西王禿髮利鹿孤寢疾，遣令以國事授弟辱檀。

translations.literal: King Lilugu of Hexi lay gravely ill and ordered that state affairs be handed to his younger brother Rutuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu, King of Hexi, fell mortally ill and directed that the affairs of state be entrusted to his younger brother Rutuan.

sentences.zh: 初，禿髮思復鞬愛重辱檀，謂諸子曰：「辱檀器識，非汝曹所及也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Tufa Sifujian had loved and esteemed Rutuan and said to his sons: "Rutuan in talent and judgment is beyond what you can match."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Tufa Sifujian had favored Rutuan and told his sons: "In talent and judgment Rutuan is beyond any of you."

sentences.zh: 故諸兄不以傳子而傳於弟。

translations.literal: Therefore the elder brothers did not pass the succession to sons but to a younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: So the elder brothers passed the throne not to their sons but to their younger brother.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤在位，垂拱而已，軍國大事皆委於辱檀。

translations.literal: While Lilugu held the throne, he merely folded his hands; all great matters of army and state were entrusted to Rutuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu reigned in name only, hands at ease; Rutuan handled every weighty affair of war and government.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤卒，辱檀襲位，更稱涼王，改元弘昌，遷於樂都，謚利鹿孤曰康王。

translations.literal: When Lilugu died, Rutuan succeeded, again styled himself King of Liang, changed the era name to Hongchang, moved the capital to Ledu, and posthumously titled Lilugu King Kang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lilugu's death Rutuan took the throne, assumed once more the title King of Liang, adopted the era name Hongchang, relocated to Ledu, and gave Lilugu the posthumous title King Kang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，太尉玄出屯姑孰，辭錄尚書事，詔許之，而大政皆就咨焉，小事則決於尚書令桓謙及卞范之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Grand Marshal Xuan went out to encamp at Gushu, resigned the post of recording secretary of the Masters of Writing; an edict permitted it, yet great affairs were all brought to him for consultation, while small matters were decided by Masters of Writing Chief Huan Qian and Bian Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Grand Marshal Xuan took up camp at Gushu and relinquished his role overseeing the Masters of Writing; the court assented, but major policy still came to him for counsel, while Huan Qian and Bian Fanzhi decided lesser business.

sentences.zh: 自隆安以來，中外之人厭於禍亂。

translations.literal: From Long'an onward, men within and without the court had wearied of calamity and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Long'an era, court and countryside alike had grown sick of chaos and ruin.

sentences.zh: 及玄初至，黜奸佞，擢俊賢，京師欣然，冀得少安。

translations.literal: When Xuan first arrived, he dismissed treacherous flatterers and raised worthy men; the capital rejoiced, hoping for a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xuan's arrival brought down the corrupt, lifted the able, and the capital brightened with hope of respite.

sentences.zh: 既而玄奢豪縱逸，政令無常，朋黨互起，陵侮朝廷，裁損乘輿供奉之具，帝幾不免饑寒，由是眾心失望。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xuan grew extravagant, proud, and dissolute; government orders were erratic; factions arose against one another; he insulted the court and cut the emperor's provision for the imperial carriage, so that the sovereign nearly suffered cold and hunger—whereupon all hearts lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xuan sank into extravagance and license, his edicts capricious, his cliques warring, the throne openly mocked and the emperor's table so pared that the Son of Heaven nearly went cold and hungry, and the people's faith died.

sentences.zh: 三吳大饑，戶口減半，會稽減什三、四，臨海、永嘉殆盡，富室皆衣羅紈，懷金玉，閉門相守餓死。

translations.literal: The Three Wu suffered great famine: population fell by half; Kuaiji lost seven or eight tenths; Linhai and Yongjia were nearly emptied; wealthy houses all wore silk and brocade and carried gold and jade, yet barred their doors and starved to death side by side.
translations.idiomatic: Famine ravaged the Three Wu: half the people gone, Kuaiji stripped of seven or eight households in ten, Linhai and Yongjia all but depopulated, while the rich still dressed in silk and hoarded gold and jade behind barred gates until they starved together.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐自西平逃歸苑川，南涼王辱檀歸其妻子。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan fled from Xiping back to Yuanchuan; the Southern Liang king Rutuan returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan escaped from Xiping to Yuanchuan, and Rutuan of Southern Liang sent back his family.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸使熾磐入朝於秦，秦主興以熾磐為興晉太守。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui sent Chipan to attend court in Qin; the lord of Qin, Yao Xing, made Chipan administrator of Xingjin.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui dispatched Chipan to Qin, and Yao Xing appointed him administrator of Xingjin.

sentences.zh: 五月，盧循自臨海入東陽，太尉玄遣撫軍中兵參軍劉裕將兵擊之，循敗，走永嘉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Lu Xun entered Dongyang from Linhai; Grand Marshal Xuan sent Liu Yu, military adjutant of the Pacification Army, to lead troops against him; Xun was defeated and fled to Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Lu Xun advanced from Linhai into Dongyang; Xuan sent Liu Yu at the head of the pacification forces; Xun was beaten and fled toward Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 高句麗攻宿軍，燕平州刺史慕容歸棄城走。

translations.literal: Gaogouli attacked Sujun; Murong Gui, regional inspector of Pingzhou in Yan, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogouli assailed Sujun, and Murong Gui, Yan's governor of Pingzhou, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 秦主興大發諸軍，遣義陽公平、尚書右僕射狄伯支等將步騎四萬伐魏，興自將大軍繼之，以尚書令姚晃輔太子泓守長安，沒弈干權鎮上邽，廣陵公欽權鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: The lord of Qin, Yao Xing, mustered all armies broadly, sent Prince of Yiyang Ping, Right Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing Di Bozhi, and others to lead forty thousand foot and horse against Wei; Yao Xing himself followed with the main host; he made Masters of Writing Chief Yao Huang assist Crown Prince Hong in holding Chang'an; Moyigan held Shanggui in temporary authority; Prince of Guangling Qin held Luoyang in temporary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing mobilized on a vast scale, sending Prince Ping of Yiyang and Di Bozhi with forty thousand infantry and cavalry against Wei while he marched behind with the main army; Yao Huang remained in Chang'an with Crown Prince Hong; Moyigan secured Shanggui and Prince Qin of Guangling Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 平攻魏乾壁六十餘日，拔之。

translations.literal: Ping attacked Wei's Ganbi for more than sixty days and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping besieged Ganbi for over sixty days and captured it.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏主珪遣毘陵王順及豫州刺史長孫肥將六萬騎為前鋒，自將大軍繼發以擊之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Wei lord Tuoba Gui sent Prince Pilin Shun and regional inspector of Yuzhou Changsun Fei with sixty thousand horse as vanguard, and himself followed with the great army to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Tuoba Gui sent Prince Shun of Pilin and Changsun Fei with sixty thousand cavalry as vanguard, then marched with the main force to meet them.

sentences.zh: 八月，太尉玄諷朝廷以玄平元顯功封豫章公，平殷、楊功封桂陽公，並本封南郡如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Grand Marshal Xuan prompted the court to enfeoff him as Duke of Yuzhang for suppressing Yuan Xian, Duke of Guiyang for pacifying Yin and Yang, while his original fief of Nan commandery remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xuan maneuvered the court to make him Duke of Yuzhang for crushing Yuan Xian and Duke of Guiyang for the Yin and Yang campaigns, retaining his original Nan commandery as well.

sentences.zh: 玄以豫章封其子昇，桂陽封其兄子俊。

translations.literal: Xuan gave the Yuzhang fief to his son Sheng and the Guiyang fief to his elder brother's son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yuzhang to his son Sheng and Guiyang to his nephew Jun.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪至永安，秦義陽公平遣驍將帥精騎二百覘魏軍，長孫肥逆擊，盡禽之。

translations.literal: When the Wei lord Gui reached Yong'an, Qin's Prince Ping of Yiyang sent fierce generals leading two hundred picked horsemen to reconnoiter the Wei army; Changsun Fei counterattacked and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong'an, Ping sent two hundred elite horsemen to scout Wei; Changsun Fei met them and took every man.

sentences.zh: 平退走，珪追之，乙巳，及於柴壁。

translations.literal: Ping retreated; Gui pursued and on yisi overtook him at Chaibi.
translations.idiomatic: Ping fell back, Gui pursued, and on yisi caught him at Chaibi.

sentences.zh: 平嬰地固守，魏軍圍之。

translations.literal: Ping enclosed himself and held firm; the Wei army besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping dug in at Chaibi while Wei closed the siege.

sentences.zh: 秦王興將兵四萬七千救之，將據天渡運糧以饋平。

translations.literal: The king of Qin, Yao Xing, led forty-seven thousand men to rescue him, intending to seize Tiandu and transport grain to supply Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched with forty-seven thousand to relieve him, planning to seize Tiandu and ferry grain to Ping.

sentences.zh: 魏博士李先曰：「兵法：高者為敵所棲，深者為敵所囚。

translations.literal: The Wei academician Li Xian said: "In the art of war, heights are where the enemy perches, depths are where the enemy traps.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, doctor of Wei, said: "By the military canon, high ground invites the enemy to roost upon you, and deep ground invites the enemy to cage you.

sentences.zh: 今秦皆犯之，宜及興未至，遣奇兵先據天渡，柴壁可不戰而取也。」

translations.literal: Now Qin violates both; we should, before Yao Xing arrives, send a special force first to seize Tiandu, and Chaibi may be taken without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Qin is committing both errors; before Yao Xing arrives, send a striking force to Tiandu, and Chaibi can be yours without a fight."

sentences.zh: 珪命增築重圍，內以防平之出，外以拒興之入。

translations.literal: Gui ordered the heavy encirclement strengthened, within to block Ping's sortie, without to bar Yao Xing's entry.
translations.idiomatic: Gui strengthened the ring of fortifications, penning Ping inside and keeping Yao Xing out.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍安同曰：「汾東有蒙坑，東西三百餘里，蹊徑不通。

translations.literal: General of Guangwu An Tong said: "East of the Fen lies Mengkeng, more than three hundred li from east to west, with no passable paths.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong said: "East of the Fen stretches Mengkeng, three hundred li with no track through it.

sentences.zh: 興來，必從汾西直臨柴壁；

translations.literal: When Yao Xing comes, he is sure to come straight from west of the Fen upon Chaibi;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing will have to come down the west bank straight to Chaibi;

sentences.zh: 如此，虜聲勢相接，重圍雖固，不能制也。

translations.literal: thus the enemy's forces will join their strength, and though the heavy siege is firm, it cannot be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: then their armies will link, and our tight siege will no longer hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 不如為浮梁，渡汾西，築圍以拒之。

translations.literal: Better to throw a floating bridge, cross west of the Fen, and build a wall to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to span the river, cross to the west bank, and wall them off there.

sentences.zh: 虜至，無所施其智力矣。」

translations.literal: When the enemy arrives, they will have nowhere to apply their wits and strength."
translations.idiomatic: When they come, they will have no room to use their strength or cunning."

sentences.zh: 珪從之。

translations.literal: Gui followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed.

sentences.zh: 興至蒲阪，憚魏之強，久乃進兵。

translations.literal: Yao Xing reached Puban, feared Wei's strength, and only after a long delay advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing reached Puban, hesitated before Wei's power, and advanced only after long delay.

sentences.zh: 甲子，珪帥步騎三萬逆擊興於蒙坑之南，斬首千餘級，興退走四十餘里，平亦不敢出。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Gui led thirty thousand foot and horse to meet and strike Yao Xing south of Mengkeng, beheading more than a thousand; Yao Xing retreated more than forty li, and Ping also dared not sally.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Gui met Yao Xing south of Mengkeng with thirty thousand men, killed over a thousand, drove him back forty li, and Ping still would not break out.

sentences.zh: 珪乃分兵四據險要，使秦兵不得近柴壁。

translations.literal: Gui then divided his forces to hold four strategic points, so Qin troops could not approach Chaibi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then posted troops on four choke points so Qin could not reach Chaibi.

sentences.zh: 興屯汾西，賃壑為壘，束柏村從汾上流縱之，欲以毀浮梁，魏人皆鉤取以為薪蒸。

translations.literal: Yao Xing encamped west of the Fen, hired ravines for ramparts, bound pine logs into rafts and released them down the Fen upstream, intending to destroy the floating bridge; Wei men all hooked them up for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing camped on the west bank, piled ravine earth into walls, and sent pine rafts down the Fen to smash the bridge; Wei soldiers simply hooked them out for fuel.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，平糧竭矢盡，夜，悉眾突西南圍求出；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Ping's grain was exhausted and arrows spent; at night he led his entire force in a breakout toward the southwest encirclement seeking escape;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Ping ran out of food and arrows; by night he hurled his whole army at the southwest of the siege to break out;

sentences.zh: 興列兵汾西，舉烽鼓噪為應。

translations.literal: Yao Xing arrayed troops west of the Fen, raised beacon fires and beat drums and shouted as signal.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing lined his men on the west bank, raised beacons, drums, and shouts in answer.

sentences.zh: 興欲平力戰突免，平望興攻圍引接，但叫呼相和，莫敢逼圍。

translations.literal: Yao Xing wished Ping to fight his way out by force, but Ping looked for Yao Xing to assault the siege and draw him out—they only shouted in concert, none daring press the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing meant for Ping to fight his way free, but Ping waited for him to storm the Wei lines; they only yelled back and forth, and no one dared close on the breach.

sentences.zh: 平不得出，計窮，乃帥麾下赴水死，諸將多從平赴水；

translations.literal: Ping could not get out; his plans exhausted, he then led his followers into the water to die, and many generals followed Ping into the water;
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, Ping led his men into the river to die, and many of his officers followed;

sentences.zh: 珪使善游者鉤捕之，無得免者。

translations.literal: Gui sent skilled swimmers with hooks to seize them; none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent swimmers with grappling hooks; none escaped.

sentences.zh: 執狄伯支及越騎校尉唐小方等四十餘人，餘眾二萬餘人皆斂手就禽。

translations.literal: They captured Di Bozhi, Colonel of Swift Cavalry Tang Xiaofang, and more than forty others; the remaining host of over twenty thousand all folded their hands and were taken.
translations.idiomatic: They took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and forty-odd more; over twenty thousand soldiers surrendered with hands bound.

sentences.zh: 興坐視其窮，力不能救。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sat watching his straits, his strength unable to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing looked on helplessly, powerless to save them.

sentences.zh: 舉軍慟哭，聲震山谷。

translations.literal: The whole army wailed in grief; the sound shook mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The entire army wept until the valleys rang.

sentences.zh: 數遣使求和於魏，珪不許，乘勝進攻蒲阪，秦晉公緒固守不戰。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace with Wei; Gui would not agree and pressed the advantage to attack Puban; Duke of Qin and Jin Xu held firm and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys pleaded for peace again and again; Gui refused and drove on to Puban while Xu locked himself in and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 會柔然謀伐魏，珪聞之，戊申，引兵還。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Rouran plotted to attack Wei; when Gui heard of it, on wushen he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran then planned a strike against Wei; hearing this, on wushen Gui turned his army homeward.

sentences.zh: 或告太史令晁崇及弟黃門侍郎懿潛召秦兵，珪至惡陽，賜崇、懿死。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Grand Astrologer Chao Chong and his younger brother, Yellow Gate Attendant Yi, had secretly summoned Qin troops; when Gui reached Wuyang, he granted Chong and Yi death.
translations.idiomatic: Informants accused Astrologer Chao Chong and his brother Yi of secretly calling in Qin forces; at Wuyang Gui had both men put to death.

sentences.zh: 秦徙河西豪右萬餘戶於長安。

translations.literal: Qin relocated more than ten thousand leading households of Hexi to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Qin moved more than ten thousand prominent Hexi families to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 太尉玄殺吳興太守高素、將軍竺謙之及謙從兄朗之、劉襲並襲弟季武，皆劉牢之北府舊將也。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Xuan killed Wu Commandery administrator Gao Su, General Zhu Qianzhi, Qianzhi's elder cousin Langzhi, Liu Xi, and Xi's younger brother Jiwu—all former generals of Liu Laozhi's Northern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan executed Gao Su, Zhu Qianzhi, Zhu Langzhi, Liu Xi, and Liu Jiwu—veterans of Laozhi's Northern Headquarters army.

sentences.zh: 襲兄冀州刺史軌邀司馬休之、劉敬宣、高雅之等共據山陽，欲起兵攻玄，不克而走，將軍袁虔之、劉壽、高長慶、郭恭等皆往從之。

translations.literal: Xi's elder brother, regional inspector of Ji Liu Gui, invited Sima Xiuzhi, Liu Jingxuan, Gao Yazhi, and others jointly to hold Shanyang, intending to raise troops against Xuan; they did not succeed and fled; Generals Yuan Qianzhi, Liu Shou, Gao Changqing, Guo Gong, and others all went to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, governor of Ji and Xi's brother, rallied Sima Xiuzhi, Liu Jingxuan, and Gao Yazhi at Shanyang to strike Xuan; defeated, they fled with Yuan Qianzhi, Liu Shou, Gao Changqing, Guo Gong, and others in their train.

sentences.zh: 將奔魏，至陳留南，分為二輩：軌、休之、敬宣奔南燕；

translations.literal: About to flee to Wei, when they reached south of Chenliu they split into two bands: Gui, Xiuzhi, and Jingxuan fled to Southern Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Heading for Wei, they reached south of Chenliu and divided: Gui, Xiuzhi, and Jingxuan went to Southern Yan;

sentences.zh: 虔之、壽、長慶、恭奔秦。

translations.literal: Qianzhi, Shou, Changqing, and Gong fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi, Shou, Changqing, and Gong went to Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪初聞休之等當來，大喜。

translations.literal: When the Wei lord Gui first heard that Xiuzhi and the others would come, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At first word that Xiuzhi's party was coming, Tuoba Gui rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 後怪其不至，令兗州求訪，獲，其從者，問其故，皆曰：「魏朝威聲遠被，是以休之等鹹欲歸附；

translations.literal: Later, wondering why they had not come, he ordered Yanzhou to search; their followers were seized and questioned why, and all said: "The prestige of the Wei court spreads far, and therefore Xiuzhi and the others all wished to submit;
translations.idiomatic: When they failed to appear, he ordered Yanzhou to hunt for them; captives from their party were questioned, and all said: "Wei's renown reaches far, and Xiuzhi's group all meant to submit;

sentences.zh: 既而聞崔逞被殺，故奔二國。」

translations.literal: but then they heard that Cui Cheng had been killed, and therefore fled to the two states."
translations.idiomatic: but when they learned Cui Cheng had been executed, they turned instead to the two other realms."

sentences.zh: 珪深悔之。

translations.literal: Gui deeply regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was filled with regret.

sentences.zh: 自是士人有過，頗見優容。

translations.literal: From this time, when scholars and officials had faults, they were largely treated with lenience.
translations.idiomatic: After that, educated men who erred often met with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀攻呂隆於姑臧。

translations.literal: The Southern Liang king Rutuan attacked Lü Long at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Rutuan of Southern Liang besieged Lü Long at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 燕王熙納故中山尹苻謨二女，長曰□戎娥，為貴人，幼曰訓英，為貴嬪，貴嬪尤有寵。

translations.literal: The Yan king Xi took in marriage the two daughters of the former Zhongshan prefect Fu Mo; the elder was □ Rong'e and was made honored lady; the younger, Xunying, was made honored concubine—and the honored concubine was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Yan took Fu Mo's two daughters; the elder, □ Rong'e, became honored lady, the younger Xunying honored concubine, and Xunying won his deepest favor.

sentences.zh: 丁太后怨恚，與兄子尚書信謀廢熙立章武公淵。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ding, resentful and enraged, joined with her nephew, Masters of Writing Xin, in a plot to depose Xi and install Duke of Zhangwu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ding, furious, conspired with her nephew Xin to depose Xi and set up Prince Yuan of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 事覺，熙逼丁太后自殺，葬以後禮，謚曰獻幽皇后。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Xi forced Empress Dowager Ding to kill herself, buried her with rites due a consort, and gave her the posthumous title Empress Xianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Discovered, Xi drove Dowager Ding to suicide, buried her with reduced rites, and titled her Empress Xianyou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊辰，殺淵及信。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, he killed Yuan and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, he executed Yuan and Xin.

sentences.zh: 辛未，熙畋於北原，石城令高和與尚方兵於後作亂，殺司隸校尉張顯，入掠宮殿，取庫兵，脅營署，閉門乘城。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Xi hunted on the northern plain; Shicheng magistrate Gao He, with the palace workshop troops, made trouble in the rear, killed Colonel Director of Retainers Zhang Xian, entered to plunder the palace, took arsenal weapons, coerced garrison offices, closed the gates and manned the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Xi hunted the northern plain; Gao He of Shicheng led palace artisans in revolt behind him, killed Zhang Xian, stormed the palace for arms, seized the arsenals, pressed the garrisons, and shut the gates to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 熙馳還，城上人皆投仗開門；

translations.literal: Xi galloped back; men on the walls all cast aside weapons and opened the gates;
translations.idiomatic: Xi rode back hard; defenders threw down their arms and opened the gates;

sentences.zh: 盡誅反者，唯和走免。

translations.literal: all rebels were put to death, only He escaped.
translations.idiomatic: he executed every rebel but Gao He, who fled.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the court granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏以庾岳為司空。

translations.literal: Wei made Yu Yue Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Yu Yue Grand Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，魏主珪還雲中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, the Wei lord Gui returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, Tuoba Gui returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗社侖聞珪伐秦，自參合陂侵魏，至豺山，及善無北澤，魏常山王遵以萬騎追之，不及而還。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Shelun, hearing that Gui was attacking Qin, invaded Wei from Canhepo as far as Chaishan and the northern marsh of Shanwu; the Wei Prince of Changshan Zun pursued with ten thousand horse but could not overtake them and returned.
