translations.idiomatic: Shelun of Rouran, learning Gui was away against Qin, raided from Canhepo to Chaishan and the Shanwu marshes; Prince Zun of Changshan pursued with ten thousand cavalry but failed to catch them.

sentences.zh: 太尉玄使御史杜林防衛會稽文孝王道子至安成，林承玄旨，鴆道子，殺之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Xuan sent Censor Du Lin to guard the Worthy and Filial Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, as far as Ancheng; Lin carried out Xuan's intent, poisoned Daozi, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Du Lin to escort Prince Daozi of Kuaiji toward Ancheng; following Xuan's orders, Lin poisoned him to death.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜所署西郡太守梁中庸叛，奔西涼。

translations.literal: Liang Zhongyong, whom Juqu Mengxun had appointed administrator of Xijun, rebelled and fled to Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhongyong, Mengxun's governor of Xijun, defected to Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞之，笑曰：「吾待中庸，恩如骨肉，而中庸不我信，但自負耳，孤豈在此一人邪！」

translations.literal: When Mengxun heard of it, he laughed and said: "I treated Zhongyong with kindness like flesh and bone, yet Zhongyong did not trust me—he only relies on his own pride. Would I be undone by this one man alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun laughed: "I treated Zhongyong like kin, yet he would not trust me—only his pride. Am I ruined by one man?"

sentences.zh: 乃盡歸其孥。

translations.literal: He then returned all Zhongyong's wife and children in full.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhongyong's entire family after him unharmed.

sentences.zh: 西涼公暠問中庸曰：「我何如索嗣？」

translations.literal: The Duke of Western Liang Gao asked Zhongyong: "How do I compare to Suo Si?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao of Western Liang asked Zhongyong: "How do I measure against Suo Si?"

sentences.zh: 中庸曰：「未可量也。」

translations.literal: Zhongyong said: "That cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyong answered: "It is not yet possible to tell."

sentences.zh: 暠曰：「嗣才度若敵我者，我何能於千里之外以長繩絞其頸邪？」

translations.literal: Gao said: "If Si's talent and capacity matched mine, how could I, from a thousand li away, throttle his neck with a long cord?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: "If Si were my equal in talent, how could I strangle him with a long rope from a thousand li away?"

sentences.zh: 中庸曰：「智有短長，命有成敗。

translations.literal: Zhongyong said: "Wisdom has its strengths and weaknesses; fate has its successes and failures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyong said, "Talent has its limits, and fortune has its turns.

sentences.zh: 殿下之與索嗣，得失之理，臣實未之能詳。

translations.literal: As for Your Highness compared with Suo Si, the reasons of gain and loss I truly cannot fully know.
translations.idiomatic: Whether you or Suo Si had the better of it, I cannot truly say.

sentences.zh: 若以身死為負，計行為勝，則公孫瓚豈賢於劉虞邪？」

translations.literal: If death in person counts as defeat and success in plan counts as victory, then was Gongsun Zan not more worthy than Liu Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: If dying counts as failure and winning by strategy as success, was Gongsun Zan not greater than Liu Yu?"

sentences.zh: 暠默然。

translations.literal: Gao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 袁虔之等至長安，秦王興問曰：「桓玄才略何如其父？

translations.literal: When Yuan Qianzhi and the others reached Chang'an, King of Qin Yao Xing asked: "How does Huan Xuan's talent and stratagem compare with his father's?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Qianzhi and his party reached Chang'an, King Yao Xing of Qin asked, "How does Huan Xuan's ability compare with his father's?

sentences.zh: 卒能成功乎？」

translations.literal: Can he in the end succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Can he succeed in the end?"

sentences.zh: 虔之曰：「玄乘晉室衰亂，盜據宰衡，猜忌安忍，刑賞不公。

translations.literal: Qianzhi said: "Xuan rides on the Jin house's decline and disorder, steals the seat of chief minister, is suspicious and cruel, and his punishments and rewards are unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi said, "Xuan exploited the Jin court's decay, seized power by theft, and rules with suspicion, cruelty, and unjust rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，不如其父遠矣。

translations.literal: In my view he falls far short of his father.
translations.idiomatic: In my view he is far inferior to his father.

sentences.zh: 玄今已執大柄，其勢必將篡逆，正可為他人驅除耳。」

translations.literal: Xuan now holds the great handle of power; his momentum will surely lead to usurpation—he is fit only to be driven out by someone else."
translations.idiomatic: He already holds real power and will surely usurp the throne—he is fit only to be removed by another."

sentences.zh: 興善之，以虔之為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Xing approved of this and made Qianzhi Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was pleased and appointed Qianzhi inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦王興立昭儀張氏為皇后，封子懿、弼、洸、宣、諶、愔、璞、質、逵、裕、國兒皆為公，遣使拜禿髮辱檀為車騎將軍、廣武公，沮渠蒙遜為鎮西將軍、沙州刺史、西海侯，李暠為安西將軍、高昌候。

translations.literal: That year King of Qin Yao Xing established Lady Zhang, a lady of bright deportment, as empress and enfeoffed his sons Yi, Bi, Guang, Xuan, Chen, Yin, Pu, Zhi, Kui, Yu, and Guo'er all as dukes; he sent envoys to invest Tufa Rutan as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu, Juqu Mengxun as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Shazhou, and Marquis of Xihai, and Li Gao as General Who Pacifies the West and Marquis of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Yao Xing of Qin made Lady Zhang empress and enfeoffed his sons Yi, Bi, Guang, Xuan, Chen, Yin, Pu, Zhi, Kui, Yu, and Guo'er as dukes; he sent envoys to invest Tufa Rutan as chariots-and-cavalry general and Duke of Guangwu, Juqu Mengxun as pacifying-west general, Shazhou inspector, and Marquis of Xihai, and Li Gao as pacifying-west general and Marquis of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 秦鎮遠將軍趙曜帥二萬西屯金城，建節將軍王松匆帥騎助呂隆守姑臧。

translations.literal: Qin's General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhao Yao led twenty thousand west to encamp at Jincheng; General Who Establishes the Staff Wang Songcong led horse to help Lü Long hold Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's pacifying-distance general Zhao Yao led twenty thousand west to camp at Jincheng, and staff-establishing general Wang Songcong led cavalry to help Lü Long defend Guzang.

sentences.zh: 松匆至魏安，辱檀弟文真擊而虜之。

translations.literal: When Songcong reached Wei'an, Rutan's younger brother Wenzhen attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei'an, Rutan's brother Wenzhen attacked and took Songcong prisoner.

sentences.zh: 辱檀大怒，送松匆還長安，深自陳謝。

translations.literal: Rutan was greatly angered, sent Songcong back to Chang'an, and apologized at length.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan, furious, sent Songcong back to Chang'an with a deep apology.
